features.name: accessory_slot
features.desc: Adds a 16th equipment slot that holds a bracelet, so a character can wear one more accessory. The extra slot also works with the Gear Swap presets, which now save and restore that bracelet. Needs the server part deployed as well as the client.

features.name: alpaca_racing
features.desc: An 'Alpaca Race' tab in the arena window (Warrior's Sanctuary) for a race run by the staff on the track of the game's own Alpaca Downhill Race (Ursun Paw Mountains). A game master opens registration on a channel (/ar open), riders join with the Join button of the tab or /ar join; the race starts 60 seconds after the 2nd rider and the chat announces the count, the time and the channel. Every rider is brought to the start line, frozen and mounted on a racing alpaca; 3, 2, 1, GO! Ride through the checkpoints in order to the finish line, following the glowing blue portal rings placed along the walkable track (a blue banner at each checkpoint, a big gate with red banners at the finish) and a trail of glowing blue lights on the ground leading to the next ring along the walkable track (around cliffs and woods; a rider who strays off the track gets lights showing the way back to it); a gold beacon on screen points to your next checkpoint and the whole course is drawn on the minimap and on the map (M); spinach and Red Bull spots give a burst of speed (Alpaca Sprint), the arrows are mud traps (Hinderers). Items and class skills are locked by the server during the race, a teleport or a portal

parts.title: Monster Race bets (Aven)
parts.desc: Every 20 minutes 8 monsters race in Aven: press 'Monster Race - bet gold' in the Alpaca Race tab of the arena window, click the Monster Race icon of the shortcut bar under the minimap, type /ar race, or talk to Kimoso (Arena Admin., by the arena merchants in Aven) to bet gold on the winner at fixed odds, watch the live ranking in the window, winnings by system mail; the Aven Event tab of the arena window shows when bets are open and when the race runs. Server: the eden-alpacarace service 0.7.5 (gold through the prop_hunt CGI ph_gold, ledger ee_mrace_bets, no binary patched).
parts.label: Monster Race bets (Aven)

features.name: archive
features.desc: Treasure Archive improvements in one feature. Search bar: name, description or item id (#12345), several words all required, case, accents and punctuation ignored, Chinese input through the IME. Race/sex filter (Any, Wearable by me, Male, Female, Human, Zumi, Anura, Ursun, Halfkin) from the item's own requirement, and quality filter (White to Purple, native colours), level and type filters, combined with the native Game/Item Mall/Owned/Reverse toggles and applied by the archive's own layout (compact grid, native order, Rate unchanged), choices saved per character. The grid fills in one go instead of one entry per frame (4 ms budget per frame), and a search skips the icons of the entries it hides. Appearance tree: Head (hats only), Face, Special, Back Gear, Body Gear, 1H Weapon, 2H Weapon, Off-Hand; the native Weapons leaf is hidden. Armor tree: Heavy, Light and Cloth Armors, Ring, Necklace, Bracelet (Accessories split by equip slot, its leaf hidden), Capes, Trophies, Enchantments, Gems (the socket gems, item type 45); Special Items: Mounts, Pets, Arcane Box, Stones, Glyphs, Legacy Sets, Title, Monster Cards, Boss Cards, NPC Cards, Place Cards (the 'Card: <name>' items of Eden Duel

parts.title: Confirm Archive all
parts.desc: Archive All asks for a confirmation in the game's own Yes / No box.
parts.label: Confirm Archive all

parts.title: Right-click to Archive Save
parts.desc: With Archive Save open, a right-click on an archivable bag item puts it in the first free slot (same checks as a drag and drop).
parts.label: Right-click to Archive Save

parts.title: Retrieve all button
parts.desc: A 'Retrieve all' button in the Treasure Archive takes every owned item of the current list (search and filters) out into the bag, one at a time, after a Yes / No box.
parts.label: Retrieve all button

features.name: arena
features.desc: Every arena rule in one feature, each part switchable on its own. Party: in the 5v5 colosseum (was 6v6) the members of one party are put on the same side. Keep party: the party survives the arena (no raid conversion, not dissolved when the match closes). No defector: no 10-minute 'Defectioner' debuff for leaving or being disconnected. 1v1: an all-class 1v1 arena with one queue and one ranking 'All Classes', class change refused while queued or in a round. Spectator: a 'Spectate' button in the arena window queues the player as a spectator of the next match of that arena (off by default, Settings > Features). Relog: a fighter who disconnects during a match that still runs is sent back into it after logging in again (server side). Player lists: in each arena tab, who waits in the queue, who fights in each running match and who watches, with a Watch button that sends you into that match as a spectator (on by default, shown once the server answers). ZoneServer + MissionServer in-memory patch (one manifest), S_Parameter 455 = 10, 1v1 schedule / ranking / text records, DLL parts (1v1 ranking tree, spectator button and camera, player lists). Replaces arena_party, arena_keep_party, arena_no

parts.title: Party on one side
parts.desc: In the 5v5 colosseum (was 6v6) the members of one party are put on the same side.

parts.title: Keep party
parts.desc: The party survives the arena: no raid conversion, and it is not dissolved when the match closes.

parts.title: No defector debuff
parts.desc: No 10-minute 'Defectioner' debuff for leaving the arena or being disconnected.

parts.title: Arena 1v1 ranking
parts.desc: An all-class 1v1 arena with one queue and one 'All Classes' ranking; class change refused while queued or in a round.
parts.label: Arena 1v1 ranking

parts.title: Arena spectator mode
parts.desc: A 'Spectate' button in the arena window queues you as a spectator of the next match of that arena (spectator camera).
parts.label: Arena spectator mode

parts.title: Arena player lists
parts.desc: In each arena tab of the arena window: who waits in the queue, who fights in each running match (both teams), who watches, and a Watch button that sends you into that match as a spectator (Watch needs the spectator part). Shown only once the server answers.
parts.label: Arena player lists

features.name: auto_altar
features.desc: Runs many Altar tries from one click, in batches (a button such as 75/200 up to x200), and shows the outcome in a result window stacked like a native window. Batch size adapts to how fast the game keeps up, to avoid freezes, and the server part prevents channel hangs during large simultaneous batches.

features.name: auto_reconnect
features.desc: Session in one feature, each part switchable in Settings > Features. Connection lost (on by default): when the PC's network drops or the server stops answering in game, a strip mid-screen (and the window title) shows the time waited while the game keeps its connections; when the network comes back the game goes on by itself, nothing is rebuilt. The feature never disconnects you by itself: the strip goes away as soon as data comes back on the game's connections. When the game really loses the session, its disconnect window has a 'Restart game' button that closes the game and opens it again on the login screen. Fast logout (former fast_logout, off by default, kept on for a player who had it): shorter countdown when you go back to character selection or change channel, 3 seconds instead of 10 (part '3-second countdown'; untick it for 5 seconds); same window, Cancel button and protections; the ZoneServer part lowers the server floor to 3 s and a client on a server without it goes back to the native 10 s. Silent relog (part 'Reconnect automatically after a drop'): after a network change in game, the game restarts and quillash back in to the same character by itself, reusing the account and

parts.title: Connection lost countdown
parts.desc: When the PC's own network drops in game, a 'Connection lost' strip (and the window title) counts down 90 s while the game waits: the same network back, the game goes on by itself; otherwise the native disconnect window.
parts.label: Connection lost countdown

parts.title: Reconnect automatically after a drop
parts.desc: When the session is really lost in game (e.g. a Wi-Fi switch), the client quillash back in by itself to the same server, channel and character instead of opening the disconnect window. The login is kept encrypted in memory and handed over encrypted (DPAPI, 2 minutes), never written in clear.
parts.label: Reconnect automatically after a drop

parts.title: Fast logout
parts.desc: Shorter countdown to go back to character selection or change channel (native 10 s); the ZoneServer part lowers the server floor to 3 s (the real wait is the longer of the two).
parts.label: Fast logout

parts.title: 3-second countdown
parts.desc: With Fast logout on, the countdown starts at 3 instead of 5 (native 10).
parts.label: 3-second countdown

features.name: boss_timers
features.desc: Named field bosses of every open-world map (the red <Title> Name bosses with a long respawn, like <Desert Eagle> Guff in The Battle of Time and Space) of your channel are shown where they spawn, on the minimap and on the map (M): a red icon when the boss is alive, grey with the countdown to its respawn when it is dead, gold when the respawn is due, blue when it is not up yet since the server started. On the map (M) the icon has 'Name - 12:34' (or Alive, Due, Not up) under it; on the minimap a dead boss has its countdown under its icon; hover any icon for the name, title, level, map and time. Bosses sharing one place are one icon ('Rax'zor +2'); bosses close together on the map (M) share one icon and one label with a line per boss, and labels are moved so that no text covers another text or an icon, at every map size. Event bosses (summoned by a map event, no timer) say 'Event' until the server has seen them, 'Alive' only once it has, 'Dead' without a countdown, and what makes them appear when the spawn data tells it; a time with ~ is learned from at least two past respawns. A '?' on the map window explains the icons; /bt prints the bosses of your map in the chat (/bt all: every map

parts.title: Boss timers on the minimap
parts.desc: Field bosses of your map show on the minimap at their spawn point: red alive, grey dead, gold respawn due, blue not up yet; hover an icon for the name, level, map and time. A Treasure Goblin also shows where it runs, with the time it has left (Treasure Goblin - m:ss), from service 0.4.0 / manifest 0.3.0.
parts.label: Boss timers on the minimap

parts.title: Boss timers on the map (M)
parts.desc: Field bosses show on the map (M) of their map with 'Name - countdown' (or Alive, Due, Not up) under the icon, a tooltip and a ? help on the map window. A Treasure Goblin also shows where it runs, with the time it has left (Treasure Goblin - m:ss), from service 0.4.0 / manifest 0.3.0.
parts.label: Boss timers on the map (M)

features.name: btn_max
features.desc: Adds a MAX button next to the + button of each skill in the skill menu, so a skill can be raised to its top level in one click instead of one point at a time. Turning the feature off brings the native buttons back at once. Needs the server part as well as the client.

features.name: buff_panel_resize
features.desc: The active-effects (buff) panels can be stretched from all four edges and corners, from a single icon up to the whole screen, and never leave the screen. Icons rearrange into columns to fill the panel, and the size is remembered. On by default, client only.

features.name: bunny_race
features.desc: Playable Bunny race built on the Halfkin base, with a female (bunny woman) and a male variant, its own class lines and racial skills, crafting profession, Mecha Armor and a Bunny Ranking. Players get it at character creation or with a Bunny Rebirth item (one per sex). Requires race_core.

features.name: camera_zoom
features.desc: Lets the camera zoom out further than the game normally allows (the distance limit is raised to 30). Turning the feature off gives back the native limit. Client only.

features.name: captcha_qol
features.desc: Quality-of-life improvements for the in-game captcha window (first phase), client only. If the game build is not recognised, the native captcha is left untouched.

features.name: card_duel
features.desc: A card game of Eden: collect cards of the monsters, bosses, NPCs and places of the game and duel other players on a 3x3 board. Right-click a player and pick Card Duel; when he accepts, a duel window opens for both: each player puts one card per turn, a card captures the enemy cards next to it when its side is higher than the facing side, the element in front gives +1 (Fire > Nature > Earth > Lightning > Steel > Ice > Fire, Light and Dark beat each other) and rare cards have skills (Pierce, Combo, Fortify, Drain, Rally, Terror). Every card you lose costs you HP like a duel (never below 1 HP, given back at the end); most cards on the board wins, or a knock-out. During the duel you cannot move, fight or use items; Forfeit gives up, logging out loses. Animated duel: cards slide in, captured cards flip, HP bars drop, the active player's side glows, a victory / defeat banner ends the duel. Card collection window (Alt+C, Escape closes it): your cards page by page with their painted monster or element picture and their tooltip, your deck of 5. New players get 5 starter cards; cards drop from the loot of the monsters of each map, and every card has a 'Card: <name>' item for the Treasure Arc

parts.title: Board games (Gomoku, Othello)
parts.desc: Right-click a player > Gomoku or Othello: an invitation window (rules, optional bet in gold, AP, EP or items), then a board window for both players, 30 s per move, give up, result and record in chat. Native sounds (start, moves, last seconds, victory, defeat; silent when the game is muted) and native green fireworks over the winner. Server: the eden-cardduel service 0.9.5 (no binary patched, bets in the card duel ledger).
parts.label: Board games: Gomoku and Othello (right-click a player)

features.name: certificate_slots
features.desc: Opens two extra certificate slots (8 and 9) for each class and saves them with the character. Without the matching client announcement the server leaves those slots empty, so older clients stay safe. Also feeds the Class Planner with the saved and open slots. Needs client and server parts.

features.name: chat_emoji
features.desc: Emojis in the chat (palette, animated emojis, chat bubbles, emoji catalogue from the Eden CDN) and, as parts of the same feature, chat badges: every chat line can show the author's class icon, level and [guild] (in green) just before the name: [icon]90 [MyGuild] Name: message. The icon is as high as the chat text (native proportions, the line never grows). Three parts (class icon, level, guild name), off by default, in Settings > Features and as check boxes in the game's own Channel Settings window (Confirm saves, Cancel forgets); the chat line is hooked while chat_emoji is on (it also removes the VIP icon text that Eden clients older than vip_perks 0.4.6 send as plain text). The client reads what it already knows: players around you (class, level, guild of their nameplate) are remembered for the session, so a player seen once keeps a badge when he speaks from far away (his guild only if seen within the last 3 days, so an old guild is never shown); in the guild channel your own guild is always shown. A player never seen yet gets no badge (the line stays native). Channel colours, item links, emojis and the clickable name are untouched. Client DLL only, no server part; repack recomme

parts.title: Class icon in chat
parts.desc: The author's class icon before his name on each chat line, as high as the chat text (also a check box in Channel Settings).
parts.label: Class icon in chat

parts.title: Level in chat
parts.desc: The author's level before his name on each chat line (players seen this session).
parts.label: Level in chat

parts.title: Guild name in chat
parts.desc: The author's [guild] in green before his name on each chat line.
parts.label: Guild name in chat

parts.title: Peer list search
parts.desc: Search bar and filters in the Peer Chnl window (Peer List): a word (name, class or location), a class, a level compared with yours and a channel.
parts.label: Peer list search

parts.title: Sound effects in chat (voice lines)
parts.desc: Sound effects (voice lines) played from the chat, chosen in the in-game Sounds panel.
parts.label: Sound effects in chat (voice lines)

parts.title: Chat timestamps
parts.desc: The time of each new chat line, like [21:42], replaces the channel tag (<Say>, <Party>, <Guild>...) in the channel colour; local time of the PC, 24-hour clock, or 12-hour with the 12h box. Same option as the check boxes Time and 12h of the native Channel Settings window.
parts.label: Time instead of channel tag in chat

parts.title: Decorated chat bubbles
parts.desc: Speech bubbles with a decorated frame (Ribbon, Flame, Frost, Leaf, Royal) for characters who unlocked a style: an item listed in the eden-chatbubbles config, a style granted by the admin or a free style. Picked with the 'Bubble:' button of the native Channel Settings window (Confirm applies); seen by every player with the Eden client, others keep the normal bubble. Needs the eden-chatbubbles service (chat_emoji server part) and prop_hunt server 0.9.1 (/brd).
parts.label: Decorated chat bubbles

parts.title: Chat macros
parts.desc: FFXIV-style chat macros: a Macros button above the chat settings button, right-aligned (hide or show it with the Macros box of the native Channel Settings window; also /macro, the Macros icon of the shortcut bar under the minimap and a key in Settings > Hotkeys) opens a Chat Macros window with 10 macros per character, each a name, up to 5 lines and an optional key (Ctrl or Alt + key). A line is plain text or /s /p /g /y /t Name (Say, Party, Guild, Zone, Whisper), an emote (/wave /thanks /angry /cheer /collapse /regret /laugh /point /dance1-3) or /wait 1-10. Lines go out as normal chat (3 s apart, 8 a minute, Zone once every 30 s, no repeat of the same public text within 30 s, word filter applied); World/Buzz chat (horn items), skills and commands are refused. Saved in eden_user.ini [chat_macros] per character. Client only, nothing to repack.
parts.label: Chat macros (lines and emotes on a key)

parts.title: Bard concerts
parts.desc: FFXIV-style Performance: a Music button above the chat settings button, right-aligned (hide or show it with the Music box of the native Channel Settings window; also /perform, the Music icon of the shortcut bar under the minimap and a key in Settings > Hotkeys) opens a Performance window; click its play box and the two letter rows of the keyboard play notes (arrows: octave and instrument) on a Harp, Lute, Flute, Bells or Drum. You always hear yourself. Characters with the Bard class unlocked (or granted by the admin) also perform for others: players with the Eden client on the same channel and map within 30 m who turned on 'Hear performances' (off by default) hear the tune about 2 s later with its rhythm; players without the client get nothing. Bells and Drum are the game's own sounds, embedded in the DLL; Harp, Lute and Flute are synthesized until the admin's samples are embedded with features/chat_emoji/tools/bard_samples.py (the tool does not deliver .wav). Needs the eden-bardconcerts service (chat_emoji server part) and prop_hunt server 0.9.1 (/brd).
parts.label: Bard concerts (keyboard instrument)

features.name: class_codex
features.desc: One window listing every class of the character's race, laid out like the admin's mockup: on the left each class on its own bar with the game's badge, its name, Lv x / max, an EXP bar with the EXP numbers and its state (Current class on a gold tag, Unlocked, Can unlock, padlock + Locked); click a class to see on the right its description from the game, How to unlock (each required level with yours in brackets, or the game's quest text) or Your progress, its Characteristics and Class Stat Bonus, and its awakening path. A 'Show locked classes' box (saved per PC) hides the classes not owned yet. Opens with the Codex button added to the title bar of the Class window, Alt+J, /codex in the chat or the shortcut bar; Escape, Close or the X closes it. Client only: everything is read from what the game already knows, nothing is sent to the server. Part 'planner' (Class planner, on by default, switchable alone in Settings > Features): a Planner button left of Codex opens the Class Planner next to the Class window - your saved build, points placed on the board but not confirmed, and a Simulate mode to plan talents, certificates (slots 1-9) and skill levels within your KPs or up to Lv 90, drawn

parts.title: Class planner (simulation)
parts.desc: Planner button left of Codex in the Class window: saved build, unsaved board points and a Simulate mode for talents, certificates (slots 1-9) and skill levels, drawn on the native talent board. Nothing is sent to the server; closing the Class window puts the saved build back.
parts.label: Class planner (simulation)

features.name: collect_all
features.desc: Adds quick bulk buttons: 'Collect all' in the mailbox, 'Delete empty mails' (also removes already-read empty mails, unread letters are kept), 'Claim all' for login rewards, and 'Receive all' at the top of the commissions window to take every finished commission one by one.

features.name: confirm_actions
features.desc: Asks before three one-click actions that cannot be taken back, in the game's own Yes / No box: Revive in the death window (back to your Soul Guardian) asks 'Revive at your Soul Guardian now?', the 'Teleport me to Aven' choice of the Guild benefits board asks 'Teleport to Aven now?', and Reset UI in the main menu (Esc) asks 'Reset the interface? Every window goes back to its default place. This cannot be undone.'. Yes does exactly what the button did before, No or Escape cancels. Each part can be switched off on its own in Settings > Features. The box closes by itself when the game moves on (revived by the countdown, another player or an arena / dungeon timer, board closed, character change), so a forced revive or teleport is never held back; Revive Here, Revival Item, Accept / Refuse Revive and every other button are untouched. Client DLL only, nothing to repack, nothing on the server. The Treasure Archive's Archive All confirmation lives in the archive feature.

parts.title: Confirm Revive (Soul Guardian)
parts.desc: Revive in the death window asks 'Revive at your Soul Guardian now?'.
parts.label: Confirm Revive (Soul Guardian)

parts.title: Confirm Teleport me to Aven
parts.desc: The 'Teleport me to Aven' choice of the Guild benefits board asks 'Teleport to Aven now?'.
parts.label: Confirm Teleport me to Aven

parts.title: Confirm Reset UI
parts.desc: Reset UI in the main menu asks before every window goes back to its default place.
parts.label: Confirm Reset UI

features.name: costume_dye
features.desc: The costume dye window gets a docked 'Dye parts' window: up to 7 parts per costume (parts 1-3 = main colours, part 4 on 12 costumes, parts 5-7 = the biggest separate pieces of the costume dye mask; 6 or 7 parts on most costumes), every costume dye of your bag for this costume type with how many you have, click a part then a dye to see it on the 3D model (nothing is used), Reset, and Apply which lists exactly the dyes that will be used before dyeing. The server stays the judge: each part is one native dye use (item checked, consumed, colour saved and shown to every player); it stops at the first refused part. The colour stays one 64-bit item value (7 palette indexes once a piece is dyed), rendered by the DLL with a baked mask texture per item. Server (in-memory patch only, ZoneServer): dye zones 1-11 on costumes. Server data: 2948 costumes that have a dye mask become dyeable (S_Item / S_ItemMall column 11 bit 28, revert clears it). Costumes without any dye area are refused before a dye is used.

features.name: crash_guard
features.desc: Crash protections and crash reports in one feature, always on, each part switchable on its own for A/B comparisons (eden_user.ini [crash_guard] guard=0 / cegui=0 / shader=0 / reporter=0, after a restart). guard: native crash guards (precise sites, wild jumps, near-null reads, invalid parameter, destroyed objects). cegui: lottery window init faults on incompatible layouts. shader: D3DX constant tables served under 2 GB and poisoned shader cache entries removed at start. reporter: crash, freeze and abnormal exit reports with the game quillash, sent at once by a separate process, session summaries. Client DLL only. Replaces cegui_null_guard, shader_guard and crash_reporter.

parts.title: Native crash guards
parts.desc: Guards on known crash sites, wild jumps, near-null reads, invalid parameters and destroyed objects.
parts.label: Native crash guards

parts.title: CEGUI null guard
parts.desc: Stops the lottery window init faults on incompatible layouts.
parts.label: CEGUI null guard

parts.title: Shader cache guard
parts.desc: D3DX constant tables served under 2 GB, and poisoned shader cache entries removed at start.
parts.label: Shader cache guard

parts.title: Crash reporter
parts.desc: Crash, freeze and abnormal exit reports with the game quillash, sent at once by a separate process.
parts.label: Crash reporter

parts.title: Memory leak watch
parts.desc: Large free blocks of the game allocator handed back to Windows (MEM_RESET) so the 32-bit client lasts longer.
parts.label: Memory leak watch

parts.title: Memory decommit (TCMalloc-like)
parts.desc: Free pages of the game allocator decommitted and recommitted on allocation, like the TCMalloc build of other clients.
parts.label: Memory decommit (TCMalloc-like)

parts.title: Replace game allocator (less RAM)
parts.desc: The game's malloc / calloc / realloc entries served by our own allocator (less RAM, the game keeps fewer free blocks).
parts.label: Replace game allocator (less RAM)

parts.title: Direct3D 9Ex (less RAM, fewer device-loss crashes)
parts.desc: The game creates a Direct3D 9Ex device: no system-memory copy of managed resources (about 150 MB less RAM) and a device that survives a reset; read at game start.
parts.label: Direct3D 9Ex (less RAM, fewer device-loss crashes)

parts.title: NT heap usage by module (diagnostic)
parts.desc: Diagnostic: the Windows (NT) heap use of each module of the game, written to the quillash.
parts.label: NT heap usage by module (diagnostic)

parts.title: No freeze when closing the game
parts.desc: Closing the game no longer hangs in its exit cleanup: the process ends within a short time limit.
parts.label: No freeze when closing the game

parts.title: Live game allocations by call site (diagnostic)
parts.desc: Diagnostic: the game's live memory blocks grouped by the code that allocated them, written to the quillash.
parts.label: Live game allocations by call site (diagnostic)

parts.title: Direct3D resources by pool (diagnostic)
parts.desc: Diagnostic: the Direct3D textures and buffers counted by memory pool, written to the quillash.
parts.label: Direct3D resources by pool (diagnostic)

parts.title: Free CPU copies of static scenery geometry (less RAM)
parts.desc: The CPU copies of static scenery geometry are freed once on the graphics card (needs Direct3D 9Ex).
parts.label: Free CPU copies of static scenery geometry (less RAM)

parts.title: Trim the working set after each zone load (less RAM)
parts.desc: Some seconds after each zone load, the game's unused memory pages are handed back to Windows.
parts.label: Trim the working set after each zone load (less RAM)

features.name: dragon_race
features.desc: Playable Dragon race, female (dragonne) and male (dragon), with its own class lines, racial skills, crafting profession, Mecha Armor and ranking. Players get it with the Dragon Rebirth item (one per sex). Requires race_core; still being validated in game.

features.name: equip_pages
features.desc: Glyph pages, costume pages and costume enchantments when inspecting in one feature, each part switchable on its own in Settings > Features. Glyph pages: five pages in the Class Glyph window (tabs and a Clear button at the top, right click a tab to rename it); a page remembers the glyph of each of the 21 class slots, per character, follows what you place, and clicking a tab puts that page's glyphs on in one server request (missing glyphs leave their slot empty and are reported in the chat; archived glyphs are taken out of the Treasure Archive first). Costume pages: Three costume pages in the costume section of the character equipment window (tabs 1, 2, 3 in the free top-left cell of the costume column, plus a Save button). A page remembers the costume worn in each of the 7 costume slots (hat, outfit, glasses, face, back, right hand, left hand), per character. Pages change only when you press Save, which is active only when what you wear differs from the active page; native costume moves are left untouched. Clicking another tab puts that page's costumes on: with the costume_pages ZoneServer patch it is ONE request (the server checks every piece, the slot rules, the bag room and the p

parts.title: Glyph pages
parts.desc: Five pages in the Class Glyph window: each remembers the glyph of the 21 class slots per character, and clicking a tab puts that page on in one server request.
parts.label: Glyph pages

parts.title: Costume pages
parts.desc: Three costume pages in the equipment window, saved with Save; clicking a tab puts that page's 7 costume pieces on (one server request with the ZoneServer part).
parts.label: Costume pages

parts.title: Costume enchantments when inspecting
parts.desc: When you inspect another player, each costume tooltip shows its enchantment (Ancient Enchantment...), as for your own costumes; the ZoneServer part adds it at the end of the inspect packet.
parts.label: Costume enchantments when inspecting

parts.title: Class presets
parts.desc: A panel next to the Gear Swap window keeps, per character and per class, a Gear Swap preset, a glyph page and a costume page. Apply now puts them on in order (Gear Swap, then the glyph page, then the costume page), and they are put on by themselves when you change class (option in the panel). Skill bars already follow the class in the game.
parts.label: Class presets

features.name: equip_smooth
features.desc: Removes the hitch when a well geared player equips or unequips an item, switches a Gear Swap preset or changes class. Server (ZoneServer mempatch): each equipment recompute (RefreshEQsAttr) re-runs every equipment enchant and every stat effect sent a full stat refresh, about 300 times per recompute on an end-game character; only the last, complete refresh is now sent (stats, HP and MP identical, proved and tested). Client (DLL): with Character Info open, every stat or item packet refreshed the whole sheet (values, slot icons, 3D preview), dozens of times per preset switch and hundreds of times per class change; the refresh requests made while the game runs its network commands (one task pass per frame, 0xB4EA80) now run once, natively, at the end of that same pass (a single equip with the bag and Character Info open went from 300-600 full sheet refreshes per frame to 1), and the whole answer to a Gear Swap preset runs one refresh 150 ms after its last packet (nothing dropped, never from the render), and while items keep changing over several frames the 3D preview is re-dressed once, 250 ms after the last change, instead of once per piece (stats refresh at once). The HUD (player fra

parts.title: Texture prewarm for gear swaps
parts.desc: The DLL remembers the textures your gear presets load for the first time (up to 96, per character) and loads them quietly, one per game task pass, after you enter the world, so the first Gear Swap of a session no longer stutters while the textures load. The look of your character is unchanged; untick it to go back to loading them at the swap.
parts.label: Texture prewarm for gear swaps

features.name: fame_slots
features.desc: Fame (prestige) ids 1 to 128 instead of the native 1-38, 51-59 and 81-85, for new season fames (86 and up). Server, in-memory patches only: the MissionServer creates and credits fame ids 1-128 (natively every other id is refused with 'can't find PrestigeData' and nothing is credited, so a Pay reward 'Reputation 86' took the items for nothing), the fame name of the gain message uses text 30000+id above 100, and the ZoneServer accepts AttrGainPrestigeExp effects up to 128 (natively 99). Ids 0, negative or above 128 are still refused before anything is written. No database change: the prestige table is keyed by (player_id, prestige_id). Client DLL (always on): the Fame tab of Character Info shows 1-50 under Regional, 51-80 under General and 81-128 under Special; names and descriptions above 100 come from texts 30000+id and 30200+id (the native 1809+id / 1910+id layout collides with the descriptions after 100) in the Fame tab, the Pay window and the item tooltip; a fame without its own icon (UI/uiicon/group0NN.dds, 52 exist) shows its category icon instead of crashing the client on the missing file. Test rows for the dummy fames 86, 101 and 128 (names and descriptions, client and serve

features.name: feature_settings
features.desc: Our two tabs of the game's Settings window, each a part switchable in Settings > Features. Features tab: one check box per feature and per part, saved for the next start, Restart game button. Eden Reforged hotkeys tab (former hotkeys): Settings > Hotkeys gets two tabs, 'Game' (native list) and 'Eden Reforged' (one row per keyboard shortcut of an Eden Reforged feature, rebindable, Default / Confirm / Cancel as for the game hotkeys). Replaces hotkeys.

parts.title: Features tab
parts.desc: The Features tab of the Settings window: one check box per feature and per part, saved for the next start, with a Restart game button.
parts.label: Features tab

parts.title: Eden Reforged hotkeys tab
parts.desc: Settings > Hotkeys gets two tabs, Game (the native list) and Eden Reforged (one row per Eden Reforged keyboard shortcut, rebindable).

features.name: fix_assets_feature
features.desc: Fixed client assets (layouts + character models/animations). Repairs broken or outdated assets of the pkg. On by default.

features.name: font_select
features.desc: Adds a 'Game Font' selector in Settings > UI Settings to change the game's font. Characters missing from the chosen font are drawn with a fallback font, so mixed-language text stays readable, and changing font no longer freezes the game. Client only.

features.name: gear_swap
features.desc: Equipment presets and quick equip in one feature, each part switchable in Settings > Features. Presets 4-12 (on by default): twelve equipment presets instead of three in the switch window and on the HUD (server manifest). Weapon hand pick (former weapon_slot_pick, three parts off by default, kept for a player who had them): Shift + right-click (or Shift + its hotbar key) puts a one-handed weapon in the other hand; optional quick second right-click goes to the off hand; Ctrl + left-click marks a hotbar slot as an off-hand slot (saved per character). A plain right-click stays native. Replaces weapon_slot_pick.

parts.title: Presets 4-12

parts.desc: Ctrl + left-click a hotbar slot to mark it as an off-hand slot (its key letter turns light blue, saved per character). A one-handed weapon used from a marked slot, by key or click, always goes to the off hand; anything else on it works as usual.
parts.label: Hotbar off-hand slots

features.name: golem_race
features.desc: Playable Golem race, one body for both sexes, built on the Ursun base, with its own class lines, racial skills, the Heartstone trait (DEF +5 %, Move -5 %), the Geomancy crafting profession and a stone Mecha Armor. Players get it at character creation (13th slot) or with a Golem Rebirth item. Requires race_core.

features.name: grimoire
features.desc: Blue Mage style grimoire with 838 forms. Boss forms come from your Monster Conquests achievements: every dungeon boss, Guild Boss and Rare Monster whose achievement you hold is a form you learned, past victories, party credit and GM grants included (790 shown, the Lv 91-100 ones stay hidden while the level cap is 90). A boss form gives the boss's model and texture at an ordinary monster size (612 are wearable now; the others say 'Too big for now' or 'Not wearable yet', and the window tells which ones look like another monster). The 48 Open World forms are kept: defeating such a monster in the open world may unlock it (25% per counted kill, the 6th always does). A new form says so in the chat (one line for a batch, a summary at the first login), with a short native firework out of dungeons and fights. Open the Grimoire with its icon under the minimap, /grimoire, or the Grimoire window key in Settings > Hotkeys: a category tree like the game's achievement window, tabs All / Learned / Favorites, level filter, cards with the achievement portrait (or the game's red '?' while not learned) and a detail panel. Pick a form and press Transform: with the game's own Transformation effect you t

features.name: guild
features.desc: Guild features in one, each part switchable on its own in Settings > Features. Guild icons (on by default): Adds a 4th tab 'Visual' to the guild window: previews of the current and the new emblem (64 px and real size above heads, animated), import of any picture or animated GIF, frame choice, speed, zoom and position, outline (palette or any colour, 0-4 px), transparent or coloured background, Apply and Reset. Apply sends the game's own 32x32 emblem (leader of a guild of level 3 or more, once per minute), so every player sees it, even without the DLL. When the picture is animated, it is also published as an animated icon that players with the DLL see above heads (downloaded in the background from the Eden CDN, checked by sha256, shown only while the guild keeps that emblem). The emblem buttons of the settings tab also accept any picture (png, jpg, gif, bmp, ico, tif, webp, dds) instead of a 32x32 bitmap. Option in the tab: show animated guild icons above heads. Client DLL; the animated icon upload needs the back-office endpoint (until it is deployed, Apply still sets the static emblem for everyone and the animation is shown on the leader's PC only). parts.desc: The guild warehouse holds 100 items per tab instead of 40, with drag and drop inside the warehouse.

parts.desc: The guild Town List fills itself on open, with one search panel (town, leader, merchant, goods, buildings, level) and a merchant filter.
parts.label: Town merchant search

parts.title: Guild Benefits shortcuts
parts.desc: Three icon buttons in the guild window bar, after Guild Benefits: Open Bank, Teleport me to Aven, Open Auction House. Each one does exactly what that entry of the Guild Benefits board does (same request, same fee, same confirmation).
parts.label: Guild Benefits shortcuts

parts.title: Guild emergency call
parts.desc: The guild leader gets an icon in the guild window bar: every online guild member of his channel who has the Eden client gets a Join / Decline box with a 60 s bar and the game's war horn, and is teleported next to the leader on Join (fireworks above the leader). Once per hour, only in Aven and the open world, never from or into dungeons, PvP maps or events. Needs prop_hunt server 0.9.1 (/gld) and the eden-guildcall service (server/call).
parts.label: Guild emergency call

parts.title: Family town threshold
parts.desc: A family keeps its town with 5 members online instead of 10 (MissionServer).

parts.title: GvG player counter
parts.desc: The GvG player counter shows the real number of members per side instead of drifting below zero war after war (MissionServer).

features.name: heal_stats
features.desc: Shows healing stats on the character sheet (also on other players' sheets) and displays critical heals as green numbers. The values follow gear and certificate changes. Needs client and server parts.

parts.title: Green critical heal numbers
parts.desc: A critical heal (type 8 sent by the heal_stats ZoneServer part) shows as a green heal number instead of the raw native critical style; with algorism07.dds in the pkg it gets the small green burst. Moved from eden_patch.ini [heal_stats] crit_color (old value taken once).
parts.label: Green critical heal numbers

features.name: instant_rush
features.desc: An 'Instant Rush' box in the native dungeon entrance window (InstanceDungeonControl), between Confirm and Cancel. With an Instant Rush Ticket (item 60610, Item Mall, AP) in the bag, tick the box and press Confirm: instead of entering, the server takes one ticket, counts one entry of the day for that dungeon (the native x/10, VIP +2 kept), gives the EXP of the whole dungeon at once (every monster, native level rule) and mails the loot of the bosses and of the end chest, Breaking Point loot included (main pool, BP pool, class drops, gold). 99 dungeons with a daily limit of 10 (101-127, 201-227, 701-721, 801-828; Dream of Destruction and special dungeons excluded). No limit of its own: only the native daily entries. Box unticked = native entry. Server part: the eden-instantrush service (needs the prop_hunt server 0.9.9: ph_node, ph_exp, /irs), S_Item 60610 and the Item Mall offer. Client DLL + service + data.

features.name: inventory
features.desc: Bag and bank improvements in one feature, each part switchable on its own in Settings > Features. Bag and bank columns: the Backpack Manager gets 'Inventory cols' / 'Bank cols' radios, 12 to 20 columns for the inventory and the bank, kept per player. Premium VIP bag slot (needs the server part): one more bag slot (slot 6) in the inventory and in the bank, open while the Premium VIP is active; without it the slot is locked (items already inside can still be taken out), the usual bank bag slots keep the native rental (180 days ahead per slot). Bulk use: F9 or the minimap chest opens a window to use a whole stack at once, one per interval, boxes 'until I get X', fortification resets 'until stage and ability', several stacks of the same item in a row. Multi delete: 'Delete items...' in the Bulk Use title bar (or F11) marks bag items by click or drag and destroys them in one server request after a confirmation listing them (100 at most, rare and item mall items asked twice). Auto sell: the shop 'Sell all' is widened to the categories ticked in the 'Sell options' of the Backpack Manager and reviewed before selling (protected and touched items excluded, a second confirmation for gold and

features.name: item_support
features.desc: Raises the item-support (auto-use consumables) slots from 8 to 16. A stone or buff item is used again automatically when its effect wears off; if the server refuses the attempt, the game waits and retries instead of looping. Client only.

features.name: jump_feature
features.desc: Adds air jumps and gliding to character movement. A 'Glide x.x s' bar appears above the cast bar and a sound plays when the glide starts. On by default; needs client and server parts.

parts.title: Glider (hold Jump while falling)
parts.desc: After a jump, keep the Jump key held while falling from 4 m or more: you glide down slowly (about 1 m/s, then 3 m/s near the ground, 6 s at most), steer and use skills (about 1 s after the glide starts). A small 'Glide x.x s' bar above the casting bar counts down and a short native sound plays at the start (silent when the game sound is muted). Jump does nothing while gliding and a hit drops you. Everybody sees the glide, with or without the DLL. After touching a rising slope, Jump may do nothing until the glide time is over. Server: jump_feature mempatch 0.6.1 (a knock-up above 16 m keeps the glide). Takes effect at the next map change.
parts.label: Glider (hold Jump while falling)

features.name: legendary_achievements
features.desc: Extends the Legendary achievements (the tab of Champion of the Hunt, Flawless Blade, Senior Treasure Hunter...) from level 65 to level 90 with the same rules and the same rewards as the game's own tiers (LV1~30, LV1~50, LV1~65). 29 families get two new tiers: '<name> II' = every achievement of the family from LV1 to LV80 (13 points) and '<name> III' = LV1 to LV90 (16 points); each tier keeps every requirement of the LV1~65 one and adds the family's LV66+ achievements that already exist in the game (rare monster hunts, orange crafts of the same item type, harvests, gems, trophies), only those a player can really obtain. Like the native tiers, each one gives an honor title whose bonus is active even when the title is not worn and stacks with the LV30 / LV50 / LV65 ones: 'Mythic ...' (II) and 'Eternal ...' (III) continue the native bonus of the family (weapon P-ATK & M-ATK for the weapon crafts, resistances / evasion / parry for the armours and capes, EXP & CP, stats, speed, critical damage, max HP...: +1 step per tier where the native bonus grows from LV50 to LV65, the same value again where it stays flat). 5 grand achievements (Eternal World Ender, Eternal Artisan Supreme, Eternal S

features.name: class_shortcuts
features.desc: Fixes the old 'my skills stay on my previous class' bug: after a class change the shortcut bars (F1-F10, 1-0 and their pages) could keep the skills of another class, for days, and every later class change spread them. Cause: the MissionServer only switched the bars when the client asked for it after the class packet; a class change whose client never asked (crash or disconnection right after the change) or two changes faster than that round trip left the bars of one class stored under another one, in memory until the MissionServer restarts. Server only, in-memory patch of the MissionServer: the class change itself switches the bars (the class it replaces keeps its own bars, the new class gets its own, the client is sent the new bars), and the class the client sends is no longer trusted. No client change, no database change. Bars already polluted in the database before the fix: see the GM procedure in features/class_shortcuts/STATUS.md.

features.name: fast_craft
features.desc: Makes crafting almost instant on the server: fortification, Combine, Arcane Box and Magic Box, crafting and jewel analysis all take about 1 second instead of 2 to 5. Guild-city works (Alchemy Lab, Foundry, Magic Pool, Altar summons) are also reduced to 1 second. No client DLL needed.

features.name: hot_reload
features.desc: Server tool: reloads the game's .ini data tables (14 of them) while the server runs, with no restart and no disconnection. Item stat changes are applied to items already in play, including those carried by online characters. Meant for the admin, nothing visible to players.

checklist.item: (GM) Setup: type /clone_item 60000 1 to get the Wisdom Bracelet; ideally the full Wisdom set for the set test, and a second player wearing a bracelet for the inspect and arena tests.
Bracelet slot: open Character Info -> a new slot sits above the rings and shows a placeholder picture when empty. The slot, the bracelet and its tooltip are in English (no Chinese).
Equip: drag the bracelet onto the new slot -> its icon shows, its stats are added in Character Info, and hovering it shows the full tooltip.
Set 5/5: wear the full Wisdom set and the Wisdom Bracelet -> the set counter reads 5/5 and the 5-piece bonus (M-ATK +10%) shows as its own line, not a copy of the 4-piece bonus.
Take off: right-click the bracelet, or drag it out -> it goes back to the bag and your stats go back EXACTLY to what they were (nothing left, nothing lost), no crash.
Only bracelets there: the bracelet fits only the bracelet slot, never a ring or trophy slot; rings and trophies do not fit in the bracelet slot.
Kept: wear a bracelet, then relog, change channel and change zone -> each time it is still worn with its icon, stats and set bonus.
Inspect: target another player who wears a bracelet, right-click his portrait > Show Equipment -> the bracelet shows in its cell next to the rings, and hovering it shows his bracelet's details.
Arena: in the 3 vs 3 ranking, look at the gear of a player who wears a bracelet -> the bracelet shows (bottom right cell).
Gear Swap slot: open Gear Swap -> a bracelet slot sits above the rings, with a check box next to it that is TICKED by default.
Gear Swap deposit: drop the bracelet into that slot -> it stays there. Clicking the check box turns the 'Switch' button into 'Save Settings' and does NOT trigger a switch.
Gear Swap equip: with the check box ticked, put the bracelet in, click 'Save Settings', then 'Switch' -> the bracelet gets equipped.
Gear Swap exclude: untick the check box, 'Save Settings', then 'Switch' -> the bracelet is NOT touched. Tick it again, 'Save Settings', 'Switch' -> it is equipped again.
Gear Swap kept: put the bracelet in, 'Save Settings', fully relog and reopen Gear Swap -> the bracelet is still in the page and 'Switch' equips it (try several of the 12 pages).
Gear Swap as before: the other equipment slots of Gear Swap still save and switch exactly as before, on all 12 pages.
Bracelet type: equip the Wisdom Bracelet and hover it -> it sits in the bracelet slot, the stats apply and the tooltip type reads 'Bracelet'.
Empty slot tooltip: with no bracelet worn hover the empty bracelet slot -> the tooltip reads 'Bracelet' (not 'Talent C').
Compare tooltip: wear a bracelet, then hover another bracelet in your bag -> the 'Current Equipment' comparison tooltip shows next to it. Same with a chest armour.

(GM) Enchant in the bag: type /clone_item 60002 1, right-click 'Bracelet Enchantment (Test)', left-click the bracelet in the bag, Confirm -> 'Enchant: Bracelet Enchantment (Test)' shows on the bracelet.
Enchant while worn: same as above but left-click the bracelet worn in the bracelet slot -> it gets the enchantment too.
Wrong items refused: try to put the enchant scroll, a glyph or any other non-bracelet item into the bracelet slot -> refused.
Gear Swap pages: on pages 1, 4 and 12 of Gear Swap tick or untick the bracelet box, 'Save Settings', change zone and come back -> each page keeps its own choice and swap, no crash.
Gear Swap off: untick 'Gear Swap' in Settings > Features, open the switch window, tick and untick the bracelet box, change zone several times -> no crash, no freeze.

Moved bracelet: put Niveus's Boreal Bracelet (or a Holy Bracelet) in a Gear Swap page, 'Save Settings', take it off, move it in the bag or into the Treasure Archive, 'Switch' -> it is equipped, no error in chat.
(GM) Guild town: wear a bracelet from login, press C in Aven -> it is in its slot. Enter your guild town (/visit_family_instance <guild name>) and press C -> still worn with the same stats.
Equip then enter the town: log in with the bracelet in the bag, equip it in Aven, enter your guild town, press C -> it is worn and shown. Relog inside the town, press C -> still there.
Inspect in the guild town: two characters of the same guild, both wearing bracelets -> in Aven and then in the guild town each sees the other's bracelet with Show Equipment. Write down both channels.
Feature off: untick 'Accessory Slot' in Settings > Features -> the bracelet slot in Character Info and the bracelet box of Gear Swap are hidden; tick it again -> they come back.
Other player sees it on: a second player inspects you right after you equip a bracelet -> he sees it in the bracelet cell with its tooltip.
Bracelet with a full bag: with a full bag, right-click the worn bracelet -> it is not taken off (or the game says the bag is full); the bracelet is never lost.
Death: die while wearing a bracelet, then revive -> it is still worn, with the same stats and set bonus.
Trade a bracelet: trade a Wisdom Bracelet to another player -> he can wear it in his own bracelet slot and gets its stats.
Party: a party member looks at your equipment -> he sees your bracelet in its cell with its tooltip.
Spam equip: drag the bracelet onto its slot and right-click it several times very fast -> it ends worn or in the bag, never lost or doubled.
Option kept: untick 'Accessory Slot', relog -> it is still unticked and Character Info has no bracelet slot.
Feature off, bracelet worn: untick 'Accessory Slot' while wearing a bracelet, tick it again -> the bracelet is still worn with its stats.

/api/features/detail/accessory_slot/clie.name: accessory_slot

client.description: Adds a 16th equipment slot that holds a bracelet, so a character can wear one more accessory. The extra slot also works with the Gear Swap presets, which now save and restore that bracelet. Needs the server part deployed as well as the client.

/api/features/detail/accessory_slot/clie.changelog:
# accessory_slot — Changelog

## [0.8.12] - 2026-11-05 — system feature: always on
- registry.c row `configurable 1 -> 0` (admin request 2026-11-05): the bracelet slot is part of how the game
  works and must never be turned off. `eden_patch.ini [Features] accessory_slot=0` is ignored, the tool and the
  Settings > Features tab can no longer turn it off; the tab shows `Accessory Slot v0.8.12 (system, always on)`.
## [0.8.11] - 2026-11-03 — client: set 297 back to the native line (no bracelet, no 5-piece bonus)
- `client/assets/data/C_EquipSet__297.bin` = the native line given by NellThistle for the RFG client:
  `297|<name>|||||||||26491|26492|26483|26484|26508||26509||`. Field 9 (member 60000, Wisdom Bracelet) and field
  17 (5-piece carrier 60001, "5-Piece Effect: M-ATK +10%") are empty. The 5-piece bonus was only an example and
  still showed in the set tooltip of the main client. The tool's Install client items replaced any edited line
  with the shipped `.bin`, so removing the line by hand did not last. The name bytes are kept as they are in the
  RFG client (`EF BF BD` sequences), so the shipped line is identical to the client's and the tool no longer
  rewrites it.
- Not changed: `server/records/S_EquipSet__297.bin` still lists 60000 and 60001. The server record is insert-only
  (a different row on a server = conflict, nothing written), so the server row is edited on each server by hand.

## [0.8.10] - 2026-10-28 — client: wiring probe written at log level 1; server deploy.py status fixes
- Client: every slot-16 wiring outcome is logged with the tag `[as_probe]` (not a feature name, so it is written at
  the default log level 1; the `[accessory_slot]` tag was dropped there: 0 lines in the admin's quillash of 28/10):
  `EquipmentWnd: Slot10 wired as cell 16`, `OtherEquipmentWnd: Slot23 wired as cell 16`, or `NOT wired` with the
  reason (cell not found, widget unreadable, vtable, method refused), windows wired by the late pass, and the item id
  the server gave in loc 16 for the own window. 32 lines at most per session.
- Server `deploy.py status`: launcher state `on_disk` counts as covered; the running version is compared with the
  installed `eden_mempatch/accessory_slot.json` (fallback: the folder's manifest) and a newer folder manifest says
  "Deploy first, then restart"; when `/proc/<pid>/exe` cannot be read (status not run as root) the name comes from
  `cmdline`/`comm` with a note, and a list that cannot be read says so instead of "no ZoneServer process".
- Correction of 0.8.9 notes: GT = the guild town on node 501/502 (not 774); the RFG `otherequipmentwnd.layout` has
  `Slot23` with ID 12, cell 16 exists only through the DLL, so an empty inspect cell is not proof of a server cause.
- Tests: `client/tests/run_tests.py` 65/65 + 6 static checks; `server/test_coverage.py` 21/21; `tests.json`: inspect
  through "Show Equipment", guild town entry steps, relog check.

## [0.8.9] - 2026-10-28 — server deploy.py: status checks every running server holds slot 16
- `deploy.py status` lists each running ZoneServer*/MissionServer* process with the launcher report of the same pid:
  `[running] ZoneServerCh3 pid N : accessory_slot 0.8.4 applied`, or `[UNPATCHED]` when the process was started outside
  the launcher, launched without the manifest, refused by it, or still holds an older manifest version (restart
  needed). A warning says that players on such a server see the bracelet slot empty. STATE is unchanged.
- Investigation of the live report "bracelets not visible in GT" (Guild Town): see STATUS.md (28/10). Client unchanged.
- Client test bench (`client/tests/run_tests.py`): `test_route.exe` is linked without ASLR (`--disable-dynamicbase`).
  With ASLR Windows could load it above 0x1200000, the code-range guard of `module_vmethod` then refused the fake
  window vtable and 5 bracelet-route checks failed at random (ops run of 28/10 21:53; reproduced with an image base of
  0x13000000: the same 5 failures). Game code unchanged (game_.exe is fixed at 0x400000).
- Tests: `server/test_coverage.py` 10/10; `tests.json` +2 in-game checks (own window and inspection in the Guild Town).

## [0.8.8] - 2026-10-26 — client: idle on an unknown game build; bracelet drop only into a real slot-16 cell
- Build check before anything is laid: the 10 hooked functions are compared on their first 9-16 bytes (prologue plus
  SEH handler push or first instructions, no longer `55 8B EC` alone) and the 3 patched sites on their surrounding
  instructions (Gear Swap whitelist `cmp ebx,0Fh / ja` at 0xA420E6, tooltip `lea edx,[esi-0Bh] / cmp edx,4 / ja` at
  0xA3EAE9, `call sub_8965A0` at 0x8A5D65 checked by its target). Any difference: no hook, no byte written, one
  `[feature_init]` line, the feature stays idle, also when turned on again in game. Hooks are laid with
  `eden_install_inline_hook_verified` on the same bytes.
- Before: a lone 0x0F at 0xA420E8, any `E8` at 0x8A5D65 or `83 FA 04` at 0xA3EAEC was enough to write into the code
  of another build, and the shutdown wrote 0x0F at 0xA420E8 whenever it read 0x10, patched by us or not. The
  shutdown now puts back only the byte it wrote.
- Gear Swap drop router: a bracelet goes to cell 16 only when the window has a slot-16 cell registered
  (`getSlotByID(16)`, vtable+48). A Gear Swap layout without `Weapon1/Slot10` (original or older pkg) leaves the drop
  to the game (message 812) instead of storing the bracelet in a cell nobody sees; said once at level 1.
- Tests: `client/tests/run_tests.py` 56/56 (new: the real game_.exe passes the gate, another SEH handler is refused,
  whitelist/tooltip/compare sites refused without their context, the shutdown never writes a byte it did not patch,
  an idle init writes nothing, a window without a slot-16 cell keeps the native route).

checklist.item: Alpaca Race tab: open the arena window (Warrior's Sanctuary) -> click the 'Alpaca Race' tab -> you see the race status, the rules, the course picture and the Join and Status buttons.
No race open: on the Alpaca Race tab click Status (or type /ar status) -> the chat says no race is open right now, the tab says 'No race open right now' and Join is greyed out.
(GM) Open a race: type /ar open -> every player on that channel gets a chat line that registration is open on that channel (0/10 riders) with the course name.
Join: while a race is open, click Join on the Alpaca Race tab (or type /ar join) -> the chat says you joined (1/10) and the Join button becomes Cancel.
Countdown: when a 2nd rider joins -> a 60 s countdown starts and the chat announces it at 30, 10 and 5 s with the number of riders and the channel.
Start line: when the countdown ends -> every rider is brought to the start line in Ursun Paw Mountains, each on his own place, mounted on a racing alpaca and frozen for a few seconds (3, 2, 1, GO!).
Race screen: at GO you can ride -> the top of the screen shows the race time, 'Checkpoint 0/4', your place and the time left; a live ranking window on the right updates every 1-2 s.
Checkpoints: ride through the rings in order -> the rings along the track are glowing blue (not purple) by day and by night, and the checkpoint counter at the top goes up at each ring.
Portal during a race: walk into a portal or use a teleport -> you are sent back to the course with a red message telling you to type /ar leave to quit, and your alpaca comes back after a few seconds.
Finish: cross the finish line first -> every rider sees in the chat who finished first and that the others have 45 s left.
Relog during a race: log out while racing, then log back in -> you are on foot, not frozen, no racing alpaca, and your items and skills work again.
Open refused: a player who is not a GM types /ar open -> the chat says only a game master can open a race; no race opens.
Wrong channel: a race is open on another channel, press Join -> the chat tells you which channel the race runs on and to change to it first; you are not registered.
Join twice: after joining, type /ar join again -> the chat says you are already registered (with the rider count); nothing else changes.
Cancel: after joining, click Cancel (or type /ar leave) before the start -> the chat says you left the race (with the new count) and the button reads Join again.
Countdown stops: with exactly 2 riders and the countdown running, one of them clicks Cancel -> the chat says there are not enough riders anymore and the countdown stops.
Full race: with 10 riders registered, an 11th player presses Join -> the chat says the race is full (10/10) and he is not registered.
Level needed: a low level character presses Join -> the chat says the level you need to race; the character is not registered.
Late join: once the riders are on the start line, a player presses Join -> the chat says the race has already started, wait for the next one.
Status during a race: type /ar status while a race runs -> the chat gives the channel, the number of riders, how many finished and the time left.
Items and skills locked: during the race try a potion, then a class skill -> both are refused; after the race (or after /ar leave) both work again.
Ground lights: during the race -> blue glowing lights on the ground lead from you to the next ring and on to the finish, fading with distance.
Ridable path: follow the ground lights from start to finish -> they always go around cliffs, woods and the lake (Checkpoint 2 is reached from the east), never straight up a cliff.
Way back: during the race ride about 10 m or more away from the track -> within a few seconds the ground lights show a way back to the track, then follow the track again once you are on it.
Next checkpoint beacon: during the race -> a gold beacon on the screen points to your next checkpoint and moves on after each ring.
Course on the maps: during the race look at the minimap, then open the map (M) -> the whole course is drawn on both.
Speed boosts: ride over a spinach or Red Bull spot on the track -> you get a short burst of speed (Alpaca Sprint).
Mud traps: ride over an arrow mud trap on the track -> you are slowed down for a moment, then ride at normal speed again.
Second portal: during the race use a portal or teleport a second time -> this time you are taken out of the race and back on foot.
Leave mid-race: during the race click Leave on the Alpaca Race tab (or type /ar leave) -> you are out of the race, on foot, and portals and teleports work again.
Late riders: a rider who has not finished when the 45 s after the winner run out -> his race ends, he gets the result window too and is back on foot.
Channel change during a race: change channel while racing, then come back -> no racing alpaca, not frozen, items and skills work.
Clean command: if any race effect is left on you (racing alpaca, frozen), type /ar clean -> the effect is removed from your character.

Ranking window over windows: during a race open Character Info or the Quest window over the live ranking -> the game window covers it; click the ranking -> it comes back in front. The race clock stays visible.
Monthly ranking: type /ar top -> the chat lists the best riders of the month with their wins, podiums and best time.
Monthly prize: at the start of a new month, the best riders of the past month get a mail 'Alpaca Race monthly prize' with an Honor Stars Chest (claim it once).
Legend: a rider who wins his 25th Alpaca Race gets the legendary achievement 'Alpaca Racing Legend' and a mail with the legendary reward.
Unknown command: type /ar hello -> the chat says it is an unknown command and lists /ar join, /ar leave, /ar status, /ar top, /ar clean.
(GM) Stop a race: during registration or a race type /ar stop -> the chat says the race was stopped by you, every rider is back on foot and items and skills work.
Monster Race button: in Aven talk to Kimoso, the Arena Admin, by the arena merchants -> a 'Monster Race' button shows at the bottom left of his dialog, next to Close.

Monster Race window: press that button -> the 'Monster Race' window opens with the race time and a countdown ('Race of HH:MM - bets close in m:ss'), 8 monsters with portraits and odds, and 'Last winners'.
Command: type /ar race -> the 'Monster Race' window opens, the same as from Kimoso's button.
Shortcut icon toggle: click the Monster Race icon of the shortcut bar -> the window opens and the icon stays pressed; click it again -> the window closes.
Your clock: the window shows the race time in your own local time (also in 'Last winners'), while the chat lines give the time as 'HH:MM UTC'. A race runs every 20 minutes.
Window look: 8 dark rows (number, portrait, name, gold odds, your bet, dirt lane with a coloured bead), a cream band with 'Your pick', - amount +, Bet and 'Your bets'; nothing cut or overlapping.
Screen sizes: open the Monster Race window at 1280x720, then at 2560x1440 -> every text is readable and the Last call / Auto-open / Close row is inside the frame.
Pick a monster: click a monster's name -> its row gets a gold frame, the name reads '> Name' in gold and the band says 'Your pick: Name (xN.N) - 10,000 gold pays ...'.
Bet amount: press - and + -> the amount moves between 1,000 and 1,000,000 and 'pays ...' follows. Outside the bet phase (race running or finished) - and + are greyed.
Confirm box, No: pick a monster, press Bet -> a Yes/No box asks 'Bet 10,000 gold on Name (xN.N)? A win pays ... gold by mail.' Press No -> nothing happens and no gold is taken.
Confirm box, Yes: press Bet, then Yes -> your gold drops by exactly the bet, a short sound plays, the chat says 'Monster Race: bet placed: ...' and your bet shows in the monster's row.
Gold left: after a bet -> the note under the band reads 'Bet placed: <amount> gold on <monster>. Gold left: <amount>.' with the gold you really have left.
Same monster twice: bet again on a monster you already bet on in this race -> refused with a red 'You already bet on ...' line, no gold taken.
Several bets: in the same race bet 10,000 on 7 different monsters -> each of the 7 rows shows 10,000 and the band reads 'Your bets: 70,000'.
Not enough gold: try to bet more gold than you carry -> the bet is refused with a message and no gold is taken.
Outside Aven: open the Monster Race window on another map -> you can watch the race, Bet is greyed and the note says bets are taken in Aven only. Back in Aven, a bet goes through.
Trade open: with a trade window open, try to bet -> refused, no gold taken.

(GM) Game master: open the Monster Race window with a game master character -> Bet is a plain dark button and the note reads 'Game masters watch the Monster Race but cannot bet.'; no confirmation box opens.
Last call on: tick Last call in the window, close it -> about one minute before a race the chat says 'Monster Race: last call! ...', even if you never opened the window since login.
Last call off: untick Last call -> no 'last call' chat line before the next races.
Bets close: keep the window open when bets close -> it shows 'bets closed', then with sound on 3 ticks at 3, 2, 1 and a start fanfare.
Race running: during the race -> every bead runs along its dirt lane with a coloured trail and the number boxes change to 1st ... 8th as the places change.
Winner: when the winner crosses the line -> its own cry plays and the window says '<Monster> wins the HH:MM race! Next bets in m:ss'.
Winning bet: bet on the winner -> win fanfare, the note says 'You won X gold (bets Y): it comes by mail.' and ONE mail 'Monster Race winnings' arrives with exactly bet x odds gold.
Claim winnings: open the 'Monster Race winnings' mail and take the gold -> your gold goes up once by that amount; the mail cannot be claimed twice.
Losing bet: bet on a monster that does not win -> the note says 'No win this time (bets Y).' and the chat says your bets are lost and gives the next race time.
Auto-open: tick Auto-open, bet, close the window -> at the race start the window opens by itself with the 8 runners and your bet in its row.
Relog before the start: bet, log out and back in before the race starts (Auto-open ticked) -> at the start the window opens by itself, with your bet in its row and the beads moving.
Channel change before the start: bet, then change channel before the race -> the window opens on the new channel at the start and the result chat line arrives there.
Check boxes kept: change Last call and Auto-open, relog -> both keep the state you chose.
Next race: keep the window open after a race -> when the next bets open it shows the new race with a countdown, never stuck on 'in 0:00'.
Sound muted: mute the game sound in the options, watch a race with a bet -> no tick, fanfare, cry or jingle plays.
Closing: Escape, the X and Close each close the window; with the '?' help open, Escape closes the help first.
Escape order: open the Loot Tracker (Alt+L), then the Monster Race window -> the first Escape closes Monster Race, the second the Loot Tracker.
Log out during a race: with the window open, go back to character select -> nothing stays on screen; a winning bet still sends its mail.
Aven Event tab, bets: arena window > Aven Event > Monster Race while bets are open -> tag 'Bets open' (green), 'Race of HH:MM' / 'Bets close in m:ss', same time and countdown as the window.
Aven Event tab, race: keep the tab open when bets close -> 'Racing' (gold) with 'Bets closed', then 'Starts in 0:13' counting down, 'Starting now', then 'Running now'.
Aven Event tab, after: when the last runner is in -> 'Every 20 min' with 'Race of HH:MM is over' / 'Next bets in m:ss', then 'Bets open' for the next race. Each tag changes within about 3 s.
Tab button: on the Alpaca Race tab, the 'Monster Race - bet gold' button sits under the event line; switch to other tabs and back -> it shows on the Alpaca Race tab only, no empty band elsewhere.
Window key: on the character selection screen press the 'Monster Race: window' key (if you bound one) -> nothing opens; in game the same key opens and closes the window.
Monster Race option: Settings > Features > untick 'Monster Race bets (Aven)' -> the window and Kimoso's button disappear at once; tick it -> the button is back at the next talk to Kimoso.
Feature off: Settings > Features > untick 'Alpaca Racing' -> no Monster Race window, icon or Kimoso button; the rest of the game is normal. Tick it again -> they come back.
(GM) Cancel a race: type /ar mr cancel <race id> on the open race -> every bet comes back by mail; another character pressing Bet then gets 'Bets for this race are closed.', no gold taken.
(GM) Audit: type /ar mr audit -> the chat says 'no anomaly' with the totals staked, paid and kept.
Result window: when the race ends -> each rider gets a result window with every place and time, a jingle plays and he is back on foot.
Other tabs: after looking at the Alpaca Race tab, open the other tabs of the arena window -> they look and work as before.
Other NPCs: talk to any other NPC of Aven -> no 'Monster Race' button in his dialog.
Tab button: on the Alpaca Race tab press 'Monster Race - bet gold' -> the 'Monster Race' window opens.
Screen sizes, clicks: at 2560x1440 open a game window over the Monster Race window -> that game window can still be clicked.
(GM) Race info: type /ar mr info -> the chat shows the current Monster Race.
Not a GM: a normal player types /ar mr audit, then /ar mr info -> nothing is shown to him.
Two riders: two players race together -> both see the same places on the live ranking during the race.
Two riders, results: at the end of a race with two players -> both get the same result window, with the same places and times.
Party: two players of the same party join the same race -> both are registered and race as two riders; they are still in the party after the race.
Death during a race: if your character dies during a race -> after reviving you are not frozen, not on a racing alpaca, and items and skills work.
Two bettors: two players bet on different monsters in the same race -> each one sees only his own bet in the rows and in 'Your bets'.
Two winners: two players both bet on the winner -> each one gets his own 'Monster Race winnings' mail with his own bet x odds.
Winnings after relog: win a bet, log out before opening the mail, log back in -> the 'Monster Race winnings' mail is there with the same gold.
Bets kept after relog: bet on 2 monsters, relog before the race -> both bets still show in their rows and 'Your bets' gives the same total.
Spam Bet: press Bet, then Yes, several times very fast on the same monster -> only one bet goes through and your gold drops only once.
Bets closed: open the window when it says 'bets closed', pick a monster -> Bet does not take any gold.
Monster Race option kept: untick 'Monster Race bets (Aven)', relog -> it is still unticked and Kimoso has no 'Monster Race' button.
