/api/features/detail/buff_panel_resize/c.name: buff_panel_resize

client.description: The active-effects (buff) panels can be stretched from all four edges and corners, from a single icon up to the whole screen, and never leave the screen. Icons rearrange into columns to fill the panel, and the size is remembered. On by default, client only.

/api/features/detail/buff_panel_resize/c.changelog:
# buff_panel_resize — CHANGELOG

## [0.3.0] — 2026-10-08
Admin feedback on 0.2.0 (in game): "icons do not spread vertically, and there is a width limit, unlike horizontally".

**Causes (proved in IDA).**
- Width limit: the minimum size comes from the layout (`BuffWnd1.layout`, `UnifiedMinSize {{0,260},{0,60}}` on the
  `Background` template, copied to the clones `Background1/2` = `FrameWindow+0x2D0..+0x2DC`). A panel could never be
  narrower than 260 px (about 8 icons).
- Vertical spread: the native layout `sub_A0FFE0` (container `BuffWnd1+0x2A0+0x4C·i`: pane `+0x00`, `std::list` head
  `+0x30`, count `+0x34`, row gap `+0x48`; node next `+0`, prev `+4`, slot window `+0x0C`) is rows only: slot at
  (x, y), `x += width`, new row when `x + width > viewable width` (`ScrollablePane::getViewableArea` `sub_BD0850`),
  `y += height + gap`; then `setContentPaneArea` (`sub_BCF830`) with the extents. Icons per row = floor(view width /
  icon width), so a tall panel only fills its top rows.

**Fix.**
- Init cave (`0x7BBB7E`) also writes a minimum of 36 × 50 px (one 32 px icon + the pane margins 4 × 18). Every
  re-layout then sets the exact minimum from the real icon size and the real panel margins (scrollbar included):
  one icon wide, one icon high.
- New cave at the entry of `sub_A0FFE0` (9 bytes `55 8B EC 81 EC 90 00 00 00`, checked): for the two buff panels only
  (pane parent = `CEGUI::FrameWindow`, vtable `0xF3E380`, with our marker mask) the layout is done in C with the same
  iteration order as native (reverse list when the flag is set). Panel taller than wide: column layout (top to bottom,
  then next column); otherwise the native row rule. Positions are set with `setPosition` (`sub_B87BA0`) only when they
  change, content area with `setContentPaneArea`. Any other container, or any unexpected list, runs the native code.
- Overflow is defined: rows mode adds rows (vertical scrollbar), columns mode adds columns (horizontal scrollbar).
- Tooltips and right click stay on the right icon: they belong to the slot windows that are moved.
- The keep-on-screen fit also grows a panel that is smaller than its minimum.
- Host tests extended: one-icon column over the full height, two-icon column, square, full-width row, overflow,
  order, no overlap, row mode identical to the native rule, minimum size.

## [0.2.0] — 2026-10-08
Admin request: the buff panel must stretch over the whole screen width and the whole screen height.

**What limited it.** The edge cave forced the maximum width to `{0.5,0}` (half of the screen: about 1720 px on a
3440 px screen, which is where the panel stopped before the minimap) and only opened the bottom, right and
bottom-right edges. A panel sitting at 67 % of the screen could therefore never reach the left side, and the native move
(`sub_7AEA30`) refuses any step that would leave the screen, so placing it exactly at x = 0 or y = 0 by hand was unreliable.

**Fix.**
- All edges and corners are open (`FrameWindow+0x3DC` = `0x11111113`: the 8 edge bits plus marker bit `0x2`, ignored by
  `getSizingBorderAtPoint`, which identifies the buff panels). Maximum size = the full screen in both directions.
- New cave in `FrameWindow::onMouseMove` (`0xBBA6A7`, right after the sizing edge is resolved, buff panels only): the
  maximum size is set from the dragged edge so the panel can grow up to the screen border and never past it (left:
  width <= right side, right: width <= screen - left side, same for top and bottom). CEGUI clamps by itself, so the cursor
  stays on the edge.
- The 3 `User.ini` size saves of the panel (`DragSizingEnded` `0x7BA9F9`/`0x7BAA12`, game entry/UI rescale
  `0x7BAAF8`) go through a stub that first keeps the panel inside the screen (resolution change, saved size larger than
  the screen; icons re-laid out at game entry), then saves the size AND the position (sizing by the left or top edge
  moves the panel).
- Every site is checked byte for byte; all are installed or none.
- Host tests: `client/tests/run_tests.py` (bounds per edge on 11 resolutions, 200 000 random drags, fit to screen,
  native icon flow model).

## [0.1.2] — 2026-10-04

- « Les deux caves ou aucune » est désormais vrai : si la cave des bords (`0x7BBB7E`) ne peut pas être posée après celle
  de la largeur (`0x7BAAA5`), cette dernière est retirée au lieu de rester seule (panneau non élargissable avec une
  largeur figée). Aucun changement quand les deux se posent.

## [0.1.1] — 2026-10-03
Retour admin sur 0.1.0 : la largeur revenait à la forme d'origine au changement de zone et au relog.

**Cause (prouvée).** La largeur était bien écrite dans `User.ini` (`[/Background1] Size` = 733 px chez
l'admin) et relue par l'init du dialogue. Mais juste après, l'init de l'interface de jeu (`sub_7A7C80`)
appelle `sub_795270` puis `sub_794B50`, qui lancent le slot 5 de chaque dialogue ; pour `BuffWnd1` c'est
`sub_7BAA20`, qui refait `setSize({0, 160·k+29} × hauteur·k)` puis **enregistre aussitôt** dans `User.ini`.
La largeur repartait à 189 px (260 au minimum) et écrasait la sauvegarde ; la hauteur était conservée.

**Correctif.** Cave à `0x7BAAA5` (7 octets vérifiés) : la largeur construite par `sub_7BAA20` est remplacée
par la largeur courante du panneau (`getSize` `sub_B7FEB0`) avant `setSize` ; hauteur, replacement des
icônes, position et sauvegarde restent natifs. L'élargissement n'est posé que si cette cave est posée.

## [0.1.0] — 2026-10-03
Première version : panneau des effets actifs étirable en largeur, largeur mémorisée comme la hauteur.

**Cause.** L'init du dialogue `BuffWnd1` (`sub_7BB7E0`) clone le gabarit `Root/BuffWnd/Background` en
`Background1`/`Background2` et force sur chaque clone le masque de bords de redimensionnement (champ Eden
`FrameWindow+0x3DC`) à `0x1000` = bas seul (`0x7BBB7E`, `mov [esi+3DCh], 1000h`). Le coin bas-droit était
donc traité comme le bord bas.

**Correctif.** Cave à `0x7BBB7E` (octets vérifiés, pose suspendue) : masque `0x10001010` (bas + droite +
coin bas-droit) e

checklist.item: Setup: log in with a character that has a few active buffs, so the buff panel shows some icons.
One column: make the buff panel one icon wide along the left border, from top to bottom of the screen -> buffs stack in one column, none cut or overlapping.
Resize cursors: hover each edge and corner of the buff panel -> the cursor turns into the matching resize arrow. Dragging the frame away from the edges still moves the panel.
Wider: drag the right edge or the bottom-right corner of the buff panel -> it gets wider, icons fill the rows without overlapping or being cut.
Smallest: drag the right edge left as far as possible -> it becomes one icon wide. Same with the bottom edge -> one icon high.
Taller: drag the bottom edge of the buff panel down -> it gets taller as in the normal game.
Move then resize: move the panel by its top strip, then widen it -> both the place and the width stay as set.
Kept on teleport: widen the panel, then teleport -> it comes back with the same width and height.
Kept on relog and restart: widen the panel, go to character select and back, then quit and restart the game -> same width and height.
Place kept: stretch the panel by its left or top edge, then teleport, relog and restart the game -> it keeps the same place, not just the same size.
Interface size: change the interface size and apply -> no crash, the panel keeps its width and icons rewrap.
Buffs come and go: gain and lose buffs while the panel is very wide, then very tall -> icons are added and removed in the current layout.
Feature off and on: untick Buff Panel Resize in Settings > Features -> only the bottom edge resizes. Tick it again -> without relogging, any edge or corner stretches it.
Two columns: make the panel two icons wide and tall -> icons fill the first column top to bottom, then the second. A wide panel still fills rows left to right.
Same order: in a tall, narrow panel the buffs come in the same order as in a wide one (same first icon).
Tooltips and removal: in a tall, narrow panel hover each icon -> the tooltip matches it. Right-click a removable buff -> that exact buff is removed.
Too many buffs: more buffs than fit -> extra icons go to a next column with a horizontal scrollbar (tall panel) or a next row with a vertical scrollbar (wide panel).
Full width: drag the left edge to the screen's left border, then the right edge to the right border -> it covers the whole width, over the minimap, never past the screen.
Full height: drag the top edge to the top of the screen, then the bottom edge to the bottom -> it covers the whole height and stops exactly at both borders.
Corners: drag the top-left corner to the screen's top-left, then the bottom-right corner to the bottom-right -> it covers the screen. Drag back -> it shrinks normally.
Fast drag: resize the panel and drag very fast past a screen border, far outside the game window -> it stops at the border and follows again when you come back.
Other windows: with the panel not over other windows, click the minimap, skill bar and other windows -> they all work as before.
Smaller resolution: panel covering the whole screen -> switch to a smaller resolution -> it fits inside the new screen; back to the larger one -> it stays inside.
Two game windows: run two games side by side -> each stretches its buff panel to its own window borders, on its own.
Death: with a wide panel, die and revive -> the panel keeps its size and place and the buffs show again as they come back.
Off kept after relog: untick Buff Panel Resize in Settings > Features -> relog -> only the bottom edge of the buff panel resizes.
Party buffs: in a party, a member casts a buff on you while the panel is tall and narrow -> the new icon shows in the current layout.

  reachable during a Game Reset) a small wndhook handler `camera_zoom_restore` waits, every 250 ms, for the ceiling
  to come back to 30, writes the native value and removes itself. Turning the feature ON again drops it.

## server 0.9.5 (2026-10-28) - stable card catalogue, refusal reason after a service restart
- **Issued cards no longer change when the client data changes** (major): `gen_cards.py` recomputed every card from
  the monster medians of each level band and the boss ranking, so the 28/10 18:58 rewrite of
  `game_unpacked\data\db\c_monster.ini` / `c_npc.ini` (other lanes) moved the sides of 115 cards already handed out
  (e.g. 1040104 Dark Abyss Killer [3,2,3,10] -> [3,3,3,9]) and `gen_cards.py --check` turned `ops_test_feature` red.
  Now `stabilize()` keeps every card of the previous `cards.json` as it is (sides, rarity, skills, element, nodes);
  only `retired` follows the data, a card that vanished from the data stays as retired ("no longer in the client
  data"), and only brand-new ids get computed values. `--check` prints what a regeneration would add or retire.
  `cards.json` is unchanged (3719 cards).
- **NPC 54936 'Aya' (Event Organizer, placed in S031 on 28/10) gets no card** until the admin decides
  (`EXCLUDED_NPC`; removing the entry and running `gen_cards.py` adds card 2054936, nothing else changes).
- **A refused invitation is shown in the window even when the service lost the inviter's announce** (service
  restarted before his next hello): `invite()` records the board capability as soon as the command carries the DLL's
  `b:` token, so "closed for now", "right-click another player", a bet syntax error and "bets are closed" also reach
  the DLL as `bg|refused|...` instead of "No answer from the server: see the chat." after 8 s. A hand-typed
  `/card bg invite` without the token still gets the chat line only.

## server 0.9.4 / client 0.8.6 (2026-10-28) - board games: fixes from the adversarial review of 0.8.5 / 0.9.3
- **The invitation window no longer stays behind the board** (major): the service sent `inv_end|<invitee>|answered`
  before its checks and the `start` line after 2 CGI and 3 DB calls; when the DLL read them on two ticks, the window
  went idle ("Bob accepted: the game starts.") and was never closed when the game began. Then the first Escape only
  closed that hidden window instead of asking to give up, and the window showed up again when the board closed. Now
  every new game closes the invitation window (`g_bw_req` block of `cd_board_tick`), the pure `bg_wait_step`
  remembers an "answered" for 15 s (`accepted`) and closes on the `start` that follows, and service 0.9.4 sends
  `answered` only after the start lines.
- **The bet selector stays visible while the invitation waits** (major): `BetK` / `BetKA` are `DejaVu/ImageButton`,
  whose Disabled state draws only `DisabledImage`, never set: the box and its arrow vanished for up to 30 s after
  each Invite (the offline preview faked it with a grey shade). `DisabledImage` = native `ComboboxEditMiddle` /
  `ComboboxListButtonDisable`, the kind text turns grey (`7F7F7F`), Game Reset clears `DisabledImage` too; the
  preview now draws the real disabled images (static check: every image button the bet row can disable has one).
- **The red answer line goes away after 8 s** as announced: the tick that ended the note did not redraw the window
  (the redraw test read the note after it was cleared), so "Bob declined..." stayed until the next server line. Pure
  `bg_wait_redraw` (host-tested): the window is redrawn on the tick that ends the note, even inside the same 250 ms
  slot, and whenever the waiting state changes.
- **A Yes that cannot start the game is explained to the inviter**: service 0.9.4 sends `bg|refused|<reason>` then
  `inv_end|<invitee>|failed` (players too far apart, a player already busy, position unknown, bet refused, database
  error, other channel) and a chat line; the DLL shows the reason in red (or "The game could not start: see the
  chat." for a `failed` line alone) instead of "Bob accepted: the game starts." for a game that never starts.
- **GAME OVER (game the server no longer has) tells the truth**: "The server no longer has this game: it ended or was
  stopped." / "Close this window to play again." / "Bets: anything owed to you comes by mail." (it claimed "its result
  is in the chat", false after a service restart, which cancels silently), and the Othello disc counts under the
  cards are the counts of the board (they read 0/0 or the counts of an older game).
- **Game mute switch honoured**: proven in game_.exe (IDA): `client.ini [Option] SoundMute` is read by `sub_6A0FD0`
  into options `+0xCC`; non-zero = muted (`sub_784480` plays no UI sound, `sub_783710` skips the audio update,
  `sub_6A98A0` sets the music volume to 0). The board sounds are now silent too when `SoundMute` is non-zero (pure
  `bg_sound_permille`, host-tested).
- **Pale stone under a resting mouse**: the hovered square is remembered, so the pale stone also appears (within
  250 ms) when your turn starts while the mouse already rests on a playable point; before, the mouse had to leave and
  re-enter the square.
- Service: a bad `board_fx_win` value (for example "on") made `finish` raise after the end lines: bets were not
  settled and the game was not recorded; the setting is now read inside the guard (logged, game ended normally). A
  replaced invitation (the inviter invites someone else) now tells the first invitee in the chat too.
- Tests: board host tests 513 + 1 (mute), static checks 0.8.6 x7, previews 25 states (new: `othello_game_over_lost_line`,
  `invite_accept_failed`); server boards 161 (+7).

parts.label: Board games: Gomoku and Othello (right-click a player)

checklist.item: Card Duel entry: stand next to a player, right-click him, pick Card Duel -> a window offers Friendly, Ante and Hardcore; pick Friendly -> he gets a box to accept.
Collection: press Alt+C (or the Cards button at the bottom right of the menu bar) -> your card collection opens; fill a deck of 7 cards, press Save deck -> chat says 'deck saved.'.

Board: start a Friendly duel -> both see the 3x3 board and their cards. Click one of your cards, then a free square -> that card goes there. Turns alternate; a taken square or a click out of turn does nothing.
Capture: lay a card whose side is higher than the facing side of an enemy card -> the enemy card flips to your colour and its owner loses HP (bar drops). Nobody dies: HP never goes below 1.
Locked in a duel: during a card duel -> neither player can move, attack or use items.
Forfeit: in a duel press Forfeit (or Escape) -> answer No: the duel goes on; answer Yes: the other player wins.

Ante duel: two players on different internet connections, level 40+, within 10 levels, 8+ cards, in a town (e.g. Aven), both tick 'Accept staked challenges' in Alt+C -> win Ante: pick 1 captured card in 30 s.
Card drop: kill Red Cap Mushroid until it drops 'Card: Red Cap Mushroid' (about 1 kill in 70), pick it up -> the card shows in your collection (Alt+C).
Option off: Settings > Features, untick 'Card Duel' -> the Card Duel entry and the Cards button disappear; tick it -> they come back.
Gomoku invite: right-click a player next to you -> the menu shows Card Duel, Gomoku and Othello. Pick Gomoku -> a 'Gomoku: <name>' window with the rules, your record and a Bet line; press Invite.
Gomoku accept: the invited player gets '<you> invites you to a game of Gomoku. Accept?'; Yes -> a board window opens for both, black plays first, the 30 s countdown runs.

Gomoku game: play to the end -> each click puts your stone on a free point (only on your turn); five in a row wins with a gold ring on the five stones, VICTORY / DEFEAT, a chat line and the record counts it.
Othello: play Othello -> dots show only where you can play, a click elsewhere does nothing, flipped discs change colour for both, the disc count shows next to each name; most discs wins.
Othello no move: when one player has no move -> the window says so ('No move for him: play again.' / 'You had no move: your turn passes.') and the other plays again.
Give up a board game: press Escape (or X, or Give up) -> 'Give up the Gomoku game against ...?'; No: the game goes on; Yes: you lose, the other wins; after the end Escape closes the window.
Board time-outs: let your clock run out once -> a move is played for you and the window shows 'Time-outs: you 1'; a second time -> you lose ('you ran out of time').
Board bet: both in a town with 'Accept staked challenges' ticked, invite with Bet: Gold -> both lose the bet at the start; the winner gets the double by mail; a draw gives it back; Give up loses it.
Leaving a board game: log out or change channel during a game -> after about 12 s the other player wins ('<name> left').
Invite after a teleport: take a teleport or portal to another map and come back, then another player invites you to Gomoku -> the invitation reaches you.
Board games off: Settings > Features > Card Duel, untick 'Board games: Gomoku and Othello (right-click a player)' -> Gomoku and Othello leave the menu (Card Duel stays).
Board games off, invited: with the option off, another player invites you -> he gets 'cannot play board games right now' at once; you see nothing. Tick it again -> his next invitation reaches you.
Board games off mid-game: untick the board games option during a game -> the game is given up once and the window closes.
Map change during a board game: use a teleport scroll during a game -> the board window stays, the game goes on, the result reaches both players.

Bet give-up text: challenge with Bet: AP 100, start, press Escape -> the give-up question says the opponent gets your bet (100 AP); answer No. The start line says 'You play first' or '<name> plays first'.
Busy target: while a third player has a challenge waiting for the same player, challenge him too -> refused with 'is answering another challenge'.
Cards from kills: on a normal account kill monsters of a map for a while -> now and then 'you found a card: <name> (<rarity>) in <map>!' and the card is in Alt+C. Same on a GM account.
GM staked duel: a GM ticks 'Accept staked challenges' and challenges a normal player in a town -> Ante is not grey; the Ante duel starts and ends like between two normal players.
Card item: ask staff for the item 'Card: Ember Drake', use it from your bag -> it disappears, 'Ember Drake joins your card collection (Epic)!', Alt+C shows Ember Drake with its picture.
Help texts: Alt+C, click '?' -> 'Getting cards' says some items give a card when used; the Challenge window '?' says game masters can play staked duels too.
Window layering: open Alt+C, then the Quest window and drag it over -> the Quest window covers the collection; click the collection -> it comes to the front. Same with the Challenge and duel windows.
Gold bet: in the Challenge window pick Bet: Gold and 50,000 with + / -, then Friendly -> his box says 'bet 50,000 gold each'; accept -> both lose 50,000 at once; the winner gets 2 mails of 50,000.
AP and EP bets: same with AP, then EP -> both accounts lose the bet at the start; the winner's account gets both; a draw gives each his bet back; Forfeit loses it.
Bet refused: bet more gold than the other player has, or with a trade window open -> the duel does not start, the chat says why, nobody loses anything.
Escape order: open the collection, then the Loot Tracker (Alt+L), then the collection again (it comes to the front) -> Escape closes the collection first, the Loot Tracker at the next Escape.

Invitation window look: right-click > Gomoku -> board icon left of 'Gomoku: <name>', parchment with the rules, a Bet row with a 'No bet' box (each click shows the next kind), a gold Invite button and Cancel.

Board window look: start a Gomoku -> title 'Gomoku - <you> vs <him>', your card '<you> (you)' in gold, wooden 15x15 board with A-O / 1-15, a green 'Your turn - 30 s' banner, 'Give up' with a gold rim.
Waiting answer: press Invite -> the window stays open with 'Waiting for <name>'s answer (n s)'; Cancel takes the invitation back; the X only closes the window.
Declined: the invited player answers No -> the inviter reads '<name> declined the Gomoku invitation.' at once; the red line goes back to the normal text after about 8 s.
Too far apart: invite a player more than a few steps away -> the window shows in red 'Come closer to <name> to invite him.', never 'No answer from the server'.
Moved away before Yes: the players walk apart, then the invited one presses Yes -> the inviter reads in red 'The two players must stand close to each other.' and no game starts.
Inviter window after Yes: once the game starts -> the inviter's invitation window is gone (drag the board aside: nothing behind); the first Escape asks to give up.
Board sounds: chime on the invitation and at the start, a click on each stone, a tick in your last 5 s, a fanfare or a falling motif at the end; with the game muted, no board sound.
Winner stars: win a board game -> green stars float over the winner for 3 s, seen by both players.
Mouse helper: on your turn, rest the mouse on a free point -> a pale stone shows there, without moving the mouse when your turn starts; the whole square is clickable.
Othello look: start an Othello -> green felt, golden glows on the squares you can play, big disc counts next to the names.
Hardcore duel: two players who meet the Ante rules play Hardcore -> the winner keeps every card he captured (up to 5); the loser's Alt+C loses them.
Grey kinds: right-click a player who does not meet the rules (low level, too far in level, outside a town) > Card Duel -> Ante and Hardcore are grey and their tooltip says why.
Daily limit: two accounts play a staked duel, then try a second one the same day -> refused (1 staked duel per pair of accounts a day).
Deck refill: lose cards in an Ante duel, open Alt+C -> your deck is completed with your best free cards.
Duel HP: in a duel -> both start at 'HP 100 / 100'; each card you lose costs 12 HP (20 against a Drain card).
Element bonus: lay a card in front of an enemy card of the element it beats (e.g. Fire in front of Nature) -> it gets +1 on that side and can capture a card of equal value.
Leaving a duel: log out or change map during a card duel -> you lose the duel; the other player gets the win and can move again.
Item bet: type /card bet item <item id> <count>, then challenge with Bet: Item -> the other player's box shows the item; the winner gets both by mail.
Pages: in Alt+C, use the page buttons -> 'Page n / m' changes and every card shows its picture; hover a card -> its sides, element and skill in the tooltip.
New player: a brand new character opens Alt+C -> he already has 5 starter cards and can duel.
Friendly only: untick 'Accept staked challenges' -> other players can still invite you to Friendly duels and board games without bet, never to Ante, Hardcore or a bet.
Record line: after a few board games, open a new invitation -> 'Your record: W won, L lost, D drawn' matches your games.
No Card Duel on monsters: right-click a monster, then an NPC -> neither menu has a Card Duel entry.
Close the collection: open Alt+C, press Escape -> it closes; open it again and press the Cards button -> it closes too.
Duel end: play a card duel to the end -> a VICTORY / DEFEAT / DRAW banner shows, both players get their HP back and can move again.
Friendly keeps cards: after a Friendly duel both players open Alt+C -> nobody gained or lost a card.
Turn timer: in a card duel wait 40 s on your turn without playing -> a card is played for you.
Card in the Archive: put the item 'Card: Red Cap Mushroid' in the Treasure Archive (Special Items > Monster Cards) -> its slot fills.
Login screens: log out with the card collection open -> no card window stays on the login or character screens.
Deck kept: save a deck of 7, log out and back in, open Alt+C -> the same 7 cards are in your deck.
Won card kept: win a card in an Ante duel, both players log out and back in -> the card is still in the winner's Alt+C and still gone from the loser's.
Bet mail kept: win a Gold bet, log out before opening the mails, log back in -> the 2 mails with the gold are still in your mailbox.

Preview: in the certificate board, preview another class -> its slots 8 and 9 show the right certificates (not empty).
Preview edit: while previewing another class, drop a certificate in its slot 8, Confirm, then change to that class or relog -> the certificate is there.
No duplicates: a certificate already in slots 1-7 cannot be dropped into 8 or 9 (refused). One in slot 8 dragged to an empty slot 9 moves (slot 8 becomes empty).
Set bonus with green: with a 4-piece set active in slots 1-7 (4 green = +16% P-ATK/M-ATK), put a green certificate in slot 8, Confirm -> P-ATK/M-ATK must not drop. Repeat in slot 9.
Any colour: put an orange, then a blue certificate in 8 and 9 (Confirm each time) -> every set bonus of slots 1-7 stays (same stats, diamonds lit); only the 8/9 certificate's own stat is added.
Move onto a full slot: drag the slot 8 certificate onto a filled slot 9, Confirm -> it stays in 9, slot 8 is empty, the old slot 9 one is back in the list. Same after relog; also 9 -> 8.
Stability: no freeze or crash on zone change, relog or channel change; the 8/9 bonus never rolls back after relog; removing one never leaves a bonus behind or lowers your base stat.
Relog without the board: with certificates in 8/9, relog 3 times without opening the board, once onto another character, then open it -> 8/9 are right; drag and drop and right-click removal work.
Settings off: with certificates in 8/9, untick 'Certificate Slots' in Settings > Features, go to character select and back -> only the 7 normal slots, Confirm works, set bonus right, no crash.
Settings on again: tick 'Certificate Slots', go to character select and back -> your certificates are still in slots 8 and 9 with their half bonus.
Known issue: preview another class, right-click the certificate in its slot 8 to remove it, Confirm, relog -> today it comes back. Report it as known, not as a new bug.
Unconfirmed edits: change slots 8/9 without Confirm, close the Class window, reopen it -> the saved certificates are shown again (the edits are dropped).
Buff shown: put Deadly Onslaught II in slot 8 and attack until it triggers -> the buff shows in the buff bar with icon and name, tooltip P-ATK & M-ATK +5%, and in Status Info.
Debuff shown: put Critical Attack II, Shake Sonar Study II or Dragon's Roar II in slot 8 or 9 -> when it triggers, the Stun or Mundane debuff shows on the target window and in Status Info.
Double hit: put Rapier Attack II (or another Double Hit certificate) in slot 8 or 9 -> double hits in the damage chat show the certificate name.
Half text: hover Magic Lesson II in a slot 1-7 -> '10% chance to recover 10% of Max MP'. Put it in slot 8 -> '10% chance to recover 5% of Max MP'.
Two game windows: two characters, different certificates in 8/9 on each, Confirm, relog both -> each gets back its own certificates, never the other's.
Two characters: fill 8/9 on character A and Confirm, go to character select and play B -> B's slots 8/9 are empty, never A's. Back on A: A's certificates are back.
Chain of moves: A in slot 9, Confirm. Drag A to 8, drop B on 9 -> A stays in 8. Drop C on 8, drag C onto B in 9 -> 9 shows C, 8 is empty, A and B are in the list. Confirm, relog: same.
Even values: put Powerful Muscle II in slot 8 -> tooltip STR +8% and STR rises by 8% (not 7%). Put Holy Spirit Dependent II in slot 9 -> 'Received M-DMG -5%'.
Live toggle: with certificates in 8/9, untick then tick 'Certificate Slots' in Settings > Features without relogging, open the board -> 8/9 show their certificates and drag and drop works.
Empty slot: right-click the slot 8 certificate to remove it, Confirm, relog. Drag from the empty slot 8 -> nothing comes out, and no old certificate comes back in 8 or 9.
Death: with certificates in 8/9, die and revive -> they stay equipped and the half bonus is still in your stats.
Fast Confirm clicks: change slot 8, click Confirm several times quickly -> one change only, no duplicate or lost certificate, no disconnect.
Class Planner: open 'Planner' in the Class window, Certificates tab -> slots 8 and 9 show your real certificates; trying others there never changes your real slots after closing the window.
Inspected by others: player B inspects player A who has certificates in slots 8/9 -> the window opens normally on both screens, no crash.
Full restart: with certificates in 8/9, close the game completely and start it again -> slots 8 and 9 still show them and the half bonus is in your stats.
Class change with the board open: certificate board open, change class -> slots 8 and 9 now show the certificates of the new class.

client.description: Emojis in the chat (palette, animated emojis, chat bubbles, emoji catalogue from the Eden CDN) and, as parts of the same feature, chat badges: every chat line can show the author's class icon, level and [guild] (in green) just before the name: [icon]90 [MyGuild] Name: message. The icon is as high as the chat text (native proportions, the line never grows). Three parts (class icon, level, guild name), off by default, in Settings > Features and as check boxes in the game's own Channel Settings window (Confirm saves, Cancel forgets); the chat line is hooked while chat_emoji is on (it also removes the VIP icon text that Eden clients older than vip_perks 0.4.6 send as plain text). The client reads what it already knows: players around you (class, level, guild of their nameplate) are remembered for the session, so a player seen once keeps a badge when he speaks from far away (his guild only if seen within the last 3 days, so an old guild is never shown); in the guild channel your own guild is always shown. A player never seen yet gets no badge (the line stays native). Channel colours, item links, emojis and the clickable name are untouched. Client DLL only, no server part; repack recomme

/api/features/detail/chat_emoji/client?n.changelog:
## [0.47.2] - 2026-11-15 - Arabic (and every non-Big5 letter) no longer turns into ????? once sent
- Report (tester marlowmoss, 15/11): with Default (Lat RU AR) the Arabic letters show in the chat input, but the line
  sent reads `[GM]marlowmoss: ?????`.
- Cause (proved): the transport table of 0.47.0 was never installed. `ut_table()` accepted the game code table
  `0x1060A30` only if ONE `VirtualQuery` region covered its 0x60100 bytes. The table sits in `.data`: the pages the
  game writes when it loads `b2u.950` turn READWRITE, the untouched ones stay WRITECOPY, so the region is cut after
  the first page and the check failed on every client (admin quillash of 15/11, two sessions: `[unitext] game code table
  0x1060A30 not writable: chat stays Big5 only` at the first chat line). Without the table, `sub_7ADEB0` encodes every
  Arabic / Hebrew / Thai / Hangul / extended Latin letter as `?` (one `?` per letter: the 5 of the report), on send
  AND on display, for every channel (say, whisper, guild, party) and every caller of the converter.
- Fix: `ut_range_writable()` walks the table region by region (READWRITE / WRITECOPY / EXECUTE_READWRITE /
  EXECUTE_WRITECOPY accepted, guard / no-access / read-only refused); a refused table is re-checked every 5 s instead
  of switching the transport off for the whole session.
- Tests: `client/tests/unitext/run_tests.py` 146 checks: the region split is reproduced on the real `game_.exe` image
  (LoadLibraryEx, a page written then queried: the 0.47.1 check refuses, the walk accepts) and on private memory
  (a read-only page is still refused); transport round trips add marlowmoss's `U+06A7` x5, `سلام عليكم 123`,
  `Привет, как дела!`, `你好世界` and `Ça a été déjà là, ouï œuvre` (no `?` on the wire, same text back).

## [0.47.1] - 2026-11-12 - Chat icon of a Patron III bubble = the Patron III icon (badges 0.7.1)
- Report (admin, in game): Patron I and II show their icon in the chat, Patron III showed the blue diamond.
- Cause: `cn_pick` (`chat_emoji_names_core.h`) swapped the icon `S8` for `Prism` whenever the server sent tier code 2 (Patron IV, ranks 1-3 of the AP ranking) with style 8, and the picker has no Patron IV row, so the diamond appeared for a Patron III choice.
- Fix: the chat icon is always `S<style>` (the picker image); Prism now only keeps its gradient name ink. Herald (temporary title, code 1) still replaces the icon.
- Test: `client/tests/bubbles/test_core.c` checks `S<style>` for every style and tier (same image names as the picker, `S%d_%d` in chat_emoji_bubbles.c).

## [0.47.0] - 2026-11-12 - Chat in every script: Unicode transport (Arabic, Hebrew, Thai, Korean, extended Latin / Cyrillic...) + Arabic shaping and right-to-left order
- Report (tester marlowmoss): Japanese / Arabic / Thai / Chinese / Russian chat 'not working', Arabic shows `???`.
- Where it broke (measured on the game table `UIData\CodePage\b2u.950` / `u2b.950`, study
  `docs/studies/chat_unicode_transport.md`): the chat edit box is UTF-16, the submit `sub_7C86E0` converts it with
  `sub_7ADEB0` (table `0x1060A30`, reverse part `+0x40000`); every character without a Big5 code becomes `?` there
  (Arabic, Hebrew, Thai, Hangul, Devanagari, Polish / Turkish / Vietnamese letters, Ukrainian letters...). Russian
  (66 letters), kana and all GB2312 / JIS hanzi already have a code: for them the blank chat came from the FONT
  (default Arial has no CJK) -> font_select 0.8.0 glyph fallback.
- Transport: 3717 deterministic codes are written in the game table (lead 0x81-0xFE, trail 0x81-0x9F, a range the
  Big5 table never uses): EdenMods.Unicode's stable rows first (same codes for Latin-1 / Latin Ext-A, Greek, Thai),
  then Latin Ext-B, combining marks, Cyrillic + supplement, Hebrew, Arabic, Devanagari, Latin Ext Additional,
  punctuation, currency, Arabic presentation forms A (FB50-FBFF) and B, then 853 frozen symbols / CJK punctuation /
  fullwidth / jamo (`chat_emoji_unitext_extra.h`, generated once by `client/tools/gen_unitext_extra.py`, append
  only). The native encoder and decoder then carry them as 2 bytes, like a Big5 character. Any other BMP character
  (Hangul syllables, rare hanzi) is sent as two escape codes (high byte, low byte: 4 bytes) by a wrapper chained on
  the submit call `0x7C884D` (the line is replaced only when it needed an escape); on display the escapes become a
  local code (252-slot pool, trail 0x80 / 0xA0). Astral characters (emoji) stay `?`.
- Display: chat line handler `unitext` (utils/chatline, order 90, last) on the log, bubble and announce surfaces:
  escapes decoded, Arabic letters shaped (isolated / initial / medial / final, lam-alef ligatures, Persian letters)
  and every right-to-left run put in visual order (digits kept left to right, brackets mirrored, CEGUI tags never
  crossed, combining marks kept after their letter). Lines without RTL text or escapes are not touched.
- Players without the DLL: they keep seeing `?`-like garbage for the new characters (as before), never a broken
  line; nothing changes for Big5 text. quillash `[unitext] ...` (tag outside the feature names).
- Tests: `client/tests/unitext/run_tests.py` (encoder / decoder round trips Russian, Ukrainian, Thai, Japanese,
  Chinese traditional and simplified, Greek, Vietnamese, Polish, Turkish, Hindi, Arabic, Hebrew, Korean, symbols;
  Arabic shaping and order, markup, brackets, Hebrew + digits; codes frozen and identical to EdenMods.Unicode; -O0
  and -O2; sites in the source and in the real `game_.exe`), wired in `client/tests/run_tests.py`.

## [0.46.0] - 2026-11-12 - Bubble Chat V2: style icon and colour on the author's name in the chat log (badges 0.7.0, bubbles 0.5.0, eden-chatbubbles 0.5.0, eden-patron 0.1.0)
- Admin decisions (planche validated 2026-11-11, `docs/studies/bubble_chat_icon_prompts.md`): in the chat log, an icon

A line is plain text or /s /p /g /y /t Name (Say, Party, Guild, Zone, Whisper), an emote (/wave /thanks /angry /cheer /collapse /regret /laugh /point /dance1-3) or /wait 1-10. Lines go out as normal chat (3 s apart, 8 a minute, Zone once every 30 s, no repeat of the same public text within 30 s, word filter applied); World/Buzz chat (horn items), skills and commands are refused. checklist.item: Setup: in game with the chat window visible and 'Chat Emoji' ticked in Settings > Features; a second player with the Eden client next to you is needed for the rows where others see or hear it.
Relog keeps emojis: send a few :codes:, a GIF and an emoji-only line, open the palette and change page -> go to character select and back (same or other character) -> all still works, no crash.
Bubble Chat V2 for others: a second player with the Eden client picks Frost and talks -> you see the snowflake and his ice blue name; a player without the DLL sees nothing different.

Patron (DEV): the admin runs `python3 /opt/eden_patron/patron_service.py override <your idnum> 4` then relogs -> the Chat Bubble window shows Patron I/II/III unlocked; pick Patron III -> gold medal replaced by the prism icon and a cyan to m
Relog keeps emojis: send a few :codes:, a GIF and an emoji-only line, open the palette and change page -> go to character select and back (same or other character) -> all still works, no crash.
Emoji palette: click the Emoji button next to the chat input and click an emoji -> its code goes into your message.
Emoji in chat and bubble: send a message with an emoji in /say -> the picture shows in the chat line and in the bubble above your head.
Normal text: send a message without any emoji code -> it shows exactly as in the normal game.
Emoji palette: click the Emoji button next to the chat input and click an emoji -> its code goes into your message.
Emoji in chat and bubble: send a message with an emoji in /say -> the picture shows in the chat line and in the bubble above your head.
Normal text: send a message without any emoji code -> it shows exactly as in the normal game.
Graphics change: change the graphics settings and Apply, then relog -> no crash and emojis still show.
Palette search: open the palette, scroll with the wheel and the scrollbar, type 'cry' in its search box (game keys do nothing meanwhile), press Enter -> the first result goes into your message.
Animated emoji: in /say send text, a few emojis and an animated one from the Gif tab -> each shows in its place, the animated one moving; the bubble over your head shows them too.
Chat badges: tick 'Class icon in chat', 'Level in chat' and 'Guild name in chat' (Settings > Features), write in /say -> your line starts with your class icon, level and [guild] in green.
Badges from far away: with the 3 badge options on, stand near a guild mate, then go to another map -> when he writes in Guild chat, his line still shows his class icon and level.
Peer search: tick 'Peer list search', open the Peer Chnl window (P) -> type part of a player name, or pick a class, a level or a channel -> only matching players stay; 'x' shows everyone again.
Sounds panel: click the Sfx button next to the Emoji button -> the Sounds panel opens ('Click: chat input. Shift+click: preview.'); Shift+click a sound -> only you hear it.

Peer channels: Peer Chnl window, channel filter -> every channel of the server is listed in order, even empty ones; press Update -> each shows its player count, e.g. 'Ch02 (0)'; pick one -> only its players.
Sounds in Party: you and a friend with the Eden client in a party -> send a sound in Party chat -> only party members hear it; a player next to you outside the party hears nothing.

Mute a chat for sounds: in the Sounds panel row (Say, Party, Guild, Peer, Couple, Whisper, World) click Party -> it greys out, a friend's party sound no longer plays (yours still does); relog -> kept.
One sound per line: with two chat tabs that both show Party (e.g. All and a Party tab) -> send one sound -> you hear it only once.
New sounds arrive: on a PC that never played before, wait 30 s in game and open the Sounds panel -> Tom Scream, Ive got this, Faah and Emotional Damage are listed.
Mute a player's sounds: right-click a player's name in the chat -> 'Mute sounds'; he sends a sound -> you see its icon and name but hear nothing; right-click him again -> 'Unmute sounds'.
Busy chat: stand in Aven with the chat open for 10 minutes while players duel nearby (many duel and combat lines) -> no crash, the chat keeps scrolling.
Time option: chat settings button > Channel Settings -> right of 'Buzz' are 'Time' and '12h'; tick 'Time', Confirm, write in /say -> new lines start with the time, e.g. [21:42], instead of <Say>.
Time on system lines: with 'Time' on, pick up gold or accept a quest -> the system line starts with the time too; lines already in the chat keep their old look.
Time with links: with 'Time' on, send one /say line with an emoji, an item link and a chat sound -> the emoji shows, link and name stay clickable, the sound plays, the time shows once at the start.
12h format: tick '12h' too and Confirm -> new lines show the time like [9:42 PM]; relog -> both boxes are still ticked.
Time and badges: 'Time' and 'Class icon in chat' both on -> a line reads time, class icon, level, [guild], then the name; a long message on two lines has the time only on its first line.
Bubble button: Channel Settings -> the last row has 'Bubble: Classic' with a small bubble icon; click it -> a 'Chat Bubble' window opens with 6 tiles: Classic, Ribbon, Flame, Frost, Leaf, Royal.

Pick a bubble style: with styles unlocked, click the Ribbon tile -> 'Ribbon chosen: Confirm to use it.'; Confirm -> the window closes, the button reads 'Bubble: Ribbon'; your /say bubble has the Ribbon frame.
Others see your bubble: a player with the Eden client next to you sees your decorated bubble; a player without the Eden client sees the normal bubble and no strange chat line.
Every style: try Ribbon, Flame, Frost, Leaf and Royal with a short word, a long message on several lines and a message with emojis -> the frame fits, the text stays inside, emojis show.
Back to Classic: in the Chat Bubble window choose Classic and Confirm -> your next bubbles are normal again for everybody.
Macros window: click the Macros button above the chat settings button -> Chat Macros opens in the middle; each slot shows a scroll picture, its number and name; Esc closes it, no game menu.
Macros saved per character: macro 1 named Hello with lines '/p Hi team', '/wave', '/wait 2', 'Bye all'; close and reopen -> all still there; on another character the macros are empty.
Run a macro: in a party click Run on macro 1 -> 'Hi team' goes to Party, you wave (a player next to you sees it), about 3 s later 'Bye all' goes to Say; your chat channel and typed text stay.
Macro key: click the Key button, press Ctrl+Shift+2 -> it shows 'Ctrl+Shift+2'; close the window, press it -> the macro runs; press it again while it runs -> 'Macro 1 stopped.'
Refused macro lines: type '/w hello' in a macro line -> the status says '/w uses a chat horn item: not allowed in macros.' and Run refuses it; '/attack' and '/p /cd 5' are refused too.
Macro pace: a macro with 5 Say lines of different text, run it twice quickly -> lines go out at least 3 s apart, never more than 8 a minute; nobody gets the game's 'Too many messages' warning.
Party and guild lines alone: out of a party run a macro with a /p line -> 'Macro 1, line 1 skipped: you are not in a party.'; out of a guild with a /g line -> '... you are not in a guild.'
Typing in macros: type in a macro line and press Enter -> the cursor goes to the next line, the game chat does not open; click on the ground -> you can move with the keyboard again.
/macro command: type '/macro' -> the window opens; '/macro 1' and '/macro Hello' run macro 1; '/macro stop' stops it; '/macro 99' explains the usage.
Macros off: Settings > Features, untick 'Chat macros (lines and emotes on a key)' -> the Macros button and window go away and macro keys do nothing; tick it again -> back.

Macros in Mad King: Mad King Says game with 3 players, macro '/s Ready', '/wave', '/s Go' run during a silence -> Ready and Go go to Say, no wave: 'Macro 1, line 2 skipped: you are in a Mad King game.'
Macros once out of Mad King: get put out (title 'Order N - you are out, watch the others') while others still play, run the same macro -> you wave at once, Ready and Go go out, no skip note.

Performance window: click the Music button above the chat settings button (or type /perform) -> Performance opens with 5 instrument tiles (harp, lute, flute, bells, drum), the chosen one framed in gold.
Play notes: click the play box, press Z X C V B N M then Q W E R T Y U I -> you hear the notes at once; your character does not move and no skill fires; Last notes shows them.
Octave and instrument: while playing, Left / Right arrows change the octave and Up / Down the instrument; the - / + buttons do the same; Volume - / + plays a test note.
Stop playing: press Enter or click in the world -> playing stops and the game keys work again; Esc closes Performance without opening the game menu.
Hear a bard: B ticks 'Hear performances'; A (Bard class unlocked) plays near him on the same channel -> B hears the tune about 2 s later with the same rhythm; B's window says 'Hearing: A (Harp)'.
No Bard class: a character without the Bard class opens Performance -> 'Solo: only you hear your music. Unlock the Bard class to play for nearby players.' and nobody hears him.
Distance: walk 40 m away from the bard or change map -> you no longer hear him; come back close -> you hear him again.
Listen invitation: 'Hear performances' off, someone starts playing near you -> one chat line says '<name> is playing the Harp nearby...' and how to listen (at most once every 10 minutes).
Normal client: a player WITHOUT the Eden client next to the bard sees and hears nothing new (no chat line, no error).
Channel change: change channel or relog, then play again -> listening and performing still work without reopening the window.
Click away: click the play box, then click in the world (not on the window) -> the play box shows 'Click here to play: ...' again and W A S D move the character.
Enter stops: while playing press Enter -> playing stops and the chat input does NOT open; press Enter again -> the chat input opens as usual.
Perform for others off: untick 'Perform for others' and play -> 'Solo: only you hear your music ('Perform for others' is off).' and a listener next to you hears nothing.
Bubble after relog: with a style set, relog on the same channel -> other Eden players still see your bubble style.
Shortcut bar Music: the bar under the minimap has a 'Music' icon (red note) -> hover: tooltip 'Music'; click -> Performance opens and the icon stays pressed; click again -> it closes.
Esc order: open Chat Macros (/macro), then Performance (/perform) -> press Esc about 1 s apart: the 1st closes Performance, the 2nd Chat Macros, the 3rd opens the game menu.
12h greyed: Channel Settings, untick 'Time' -> the '12h' label turns grey and cannot be clicked; tick 'Time' -> '12h' works again.
VIP recruit line: a VIP party leader recruits for a multi-player dungeon (Party > Recruit) -> your Peer line reads '<Multi-Player DGN> 0/N (+V VIP), ...' with no [colour=...] or [image=...] text.
Chat at the top: drag the chat window to the top edge of the screen -> the Music and Macros buttons sit on the tab row, right of the chat window, and cover no chat line.
Padlocks: with no style unlocked, open the Chat Bubble window -> each locked tile shows a big padlock centred on the bottom of the sample bubble, covering neither 'Hello!' nor the style name.
Chat Emoji off: Settings > Features, untick 'Chat Emoji' -> codes like :smile: stay as text; a staff mark '[Reported: scammer]' and the green shield of a Thanks line still show.
Guild tag after a guild change: 'Guild name in chat' on; B left another guild and joined yours while you were elsewhere -> B writes in Guild chat -> his line shows your guild's tag, not the old one.
Old guild hidden: a player you have not seen for more than 3 days writes in World from far away -> his line shows class icon and level but no [guild]; walk next to him -> within 2 s it shows again.
Two clients on one PC: client 1 sees B after his guild change, client 2 is on another map; close client 2, then client 1, start again -> B's lines show his new guild, not the old one.
Palette Esc: open the emoji palette and press Esc -> only the palette closes, the game menu does not open.
Palette pages: open the palette and use its tabs and page buttons -> each page shows its pictures, no empty or broken squares.
One badge off: with the 3 badge options on, untick 'Level in chat' -> new lines no longer show the level; the class icon and [guild] stay.
Never seen player: a player you have never seen on screen writes in World -> his line is a normal line, no badge.
Badge boxes in Channel Settings: tick or untick the 'Class icon', 'Level' and 'Guild' boxes and Confirm -> new lines follow; change them and press Cancel instead -> nothing changes.
All badges off: untick the 3 badge options -> every new line is the game's normal line (no icon, level or guild).
Peer search off: untick 'Peer list search' -> the Peer Chnl window is the game's normal one, without the search bar.
Peer level filter: in the Peer Chnl window pick a level choice (compared with your own level) -> only players in that range stay.
Send a sound: in the Sounds panel click Ding (it goes into your chat input), press Enter in /say -> a player with the Eden client next to you sees a music icon and 'Ding' and hears it.
Sound to a normal client: a player without the Eden client next to you reads the sound as plain text and hears nothing.
Sounds in Guild: send a sound in Guild chat -> only your guild mates hear it.
Sounds in Couple and Whisper: send a sound in Couple chat -> only your spouse hears it; send one in a whisper -> only the two of you hear it.
World sounds: World is greyed at first in the Sounds panel row -> a World sound from someone is not heard; click World -> the next World sound plays.
Sound spam: send many sounds quickly -> the other player hears at most one of your sounds every 10 s and 8 per minute; the extra ones show without sound.
Others on/off: in the Sounds panel click 'Others: on' -> it shows 'Others: off' and only your own sounds play; click again -> other players' sounds play again.
Sound volume: in the Sounds panel press the volume down and up buttons -> sounds get quieter, then louder.
Muted list: Sounds panel > Muted (1) shows the player you muted; click his name -> his sounds play again.
Own name: right-click your own name in the chat -> the menu has no 'Mute sounds'.
Sounds off: Settings > Features, untick 'Sound effects in chat (voice lines)' -> the Sfx button goes away; tick it again -> it is back.
Time off again: untick 'Time' and Confirm -> new lines show <Say> again; change the boxes and press Cancel instead -> nothing changes.
Locked tiles: without any unlocked style open the Chat Bubble window -> only Classic is bright; others are dimmed with a padlock and say 'Bubble styles are given by events and the staff.' on hover.
Cancel a style: click a style, then Cancel, the close cross or Esc -> the old style stays.
Close Channel Settings: with the Chat Bubble window open, close Channel Settings -> the Chat Bubble window closes too, without a change.
(GM) Styles unlocked live: staff grants bubble styles while you are in game -> within 5 s the chat says 'Chat bubble: 5 new styles unlocked. Channel Settings > Bubble to use them.' with a short bell.
Style kept after teleport: with Ribbon set, teleport (portal or NPC) and /s hi -> the Ribbon bubble still shows and Channel Settings still says 'Bubble: Ribbon'.
Style after channel change: A (Ribbon) and B both change to channel 2 -> 10 s later A says /s hi -> B sees A's Ribbon bubble.
Late arrival: A has Ribbon; B quillash in after A -> A says /s hi -> B sees the Ribbon bubble.
Bubbles off: Settings > Features, untick 'Decorated chat bubbles' -> the 'Bubble:' button leaves Channel Settings; tick it again -> it is back.
Macro window hotkey: Settings > Hotkeys, set a key for 'Chat macros window', press it in game -> Chat Macros opens; press it again -> it closes.
Game key refused: in Chat Macros click Key and press Ctrl+1 -> refused: 'Ctrl+1 is a game hotkey (Settings > Hotkeys, Game tab). Try Ctrl+Shift+2.'
Key without Ctrl or Alt: click Key and press a plain letter -> refused with a message; the macro keeps its old key.
Macro just ran: run a macro and press its key again right after it ends -> 'Macro 2: This macro just ran: wait 5 s.'
Same text within 30 s: run a macro with the line 'Hello everyone!' twice within 30 s -> 'Macro 2, line 1 skipped: the same text was sent less than 30 s ago.'
Macro stops on travel: run a macro with '/wait 10', then travel to another map -> 'Macro N stopped (you left the world).' once; windows close cleanly and the buttons come back.
Macro after a Mad King game: 30 s after the game ends, run the same macro -> you wave and Ready / Go go to Say.
Bard with the game muted: mute the game sound in the options, play notes -> you hear nothing; unmute -> the notes come back within about 5 s.
Nobody listening: alone with 'Perform for others' on, play for 60 s -> about 2 s after the first notes 'Nobody nearby has 'Hear performances' on yet.' shows and stays while you play.
Listener count: B listens near A -> A plays -> A's window says '1 player nearby hears you (2 s late).'
Bard off: Settings > Features, untick 'Bard concerts (keyboard instrument)' -> the Music button and window go away; tick it again -> they are back.
Shortcut bar Macros: the bar under the minimap has a 'Macros' icon (scroll and quill) -> click -> Chat Macros opens and the icon stays pressed; click again -> it closes.
Music box: untick 'Music' in Channel Settings and Confirm -> the Music button by the chat goes away, the shortcut bar icon stays; same with the 'Macros' box.
Esc other order: open Performance first, then Chat Macros -> the first Esc closes Chat Macros only.
Hold Esc: open Chat Macros and Performance, then hold Esc for 1 s -> exactly one window closes and the game menu does not open.
Chat in the top right corner: drag the chat window to the top right corner -> the Music and Macros buttons go just below the tab row (known limit: they cover the first line).
12h follows Time: untick 'Time', press Cancel, reopen Channel Settings, then relog and reopen -> '12h' is greyed exactly when 'Time' is off.
Typed markup stays: a player types [colour='FFFF0000']hello in Say -> it shows exactly as typed (only the VIP recruit text is cleaned).
Bubble window Esc: open Chat Macros, then Channel Settings > Bubble -> the first Esc closes only the Chat Bubble window, the next one closes Chat Macros.
Guild tag on other chats: after B's Guild chat line shows your guild, B writes in World or Say -> his line shows your guild's tag too.
Emoji-only bubble: say a line with only one emoji -> the bubble above your head shows the emoji picture.
Emojis seen by others: B with the Eden client sees your emojis as pictures; a player without it sees the :codes: as text.
Chat Emoji back on: tick 'Chat Emoji' again in Settings > Features -> the Emoji button and the pictures come back without restarting.

Time from Settings: Settings > Features, tick 'Time instead of channel tag in chat' -> open Channel Settings: the 'Time' box is ticked and new /say lines start with the time; untick it -> the box unticks too.

Badges from Settings: tick 'Class icon in chat' in Settings > Features -> in Channel Settings the 'Class icon' box is ticked; untick the box and Confirm -> the Settings > Features option is unticked too.
Time only for you: with 'Time' on, say a line in /say -> B next to you (Eden client, 'Time' off) sees your line with <Say> as usual, not your time.
Emojis in every chat: send an emoji in Party, Guild and a whisper -> B with the Eden client sees the picture in each of them.
Mute kept after relog: mute B's sounds (right-click his name > 'Mute sounds'), relog -> B sends a sound -> you still hear nothing and 'Muted (1)' still lists him.
Macro key after relog: set Ctrl+Shift+2 on macro 1, relog -> press Ctrl+Shift+2 -> the macro runs.
Bubble style in Party chat: A (Ribbon) says a line in Party chat -> B in the party next to him sees the Ribbon bubble above A's head.
Peer search after relog: with 'Peer list search' on, relog and open the Peer Chnl window (P) -> the search bar is still there and works.
Bard after death: play the Harp, die and get revived -> open Performance and play again -> the notes play and a listener next to you hears them.

checklist.item: Setup: in game with the chat window visible and 'Chat Emoji' ticked in Settings > Features; a second player with the Eden client next to you is needed for the rows where others see or hear it.

Bubble Chat V2 (needs the eden-chatbubbles 0.5.0 service on the server): open Channel Settings > Bubble, pick Flame and Confirm, then say something in Say, Party and Guild -> in the chat log a small flame is right before your name and your name is orange on every channel; pick Classic -> no icon, native colour.
Bubble Chat V2 for others: a second player with the Eden client picks Frost and talks -> you see the snowflake and his ice blue name; a player without the DLL sees nothing different.

Patron (DEV): the admin runs `python3 /opt/eden_patron/patron_service.py override <your idnum> 4` then relogs -> the Chat Bubble window shows Patron I/II/III unlocked; pick Patron III -> gold medal replaced by the prism icon and a cyan to magenta name in the chat; `herald <char_id> 1` -> herald horn and gold name for one hour, then back to the style.
Relog keeps emojis: send a few :codes:, a GIF and an emoji-only line, open the palette and change page -> go to character select and back (same or other character) -> all still works, no crash.
Emoji palette: click the Emoji button next to the chat input and click an emoji -> its code goes into your message.
Emoji in chat and bubble: send a message with an emoji in /say -> the picture shows in the chat line and in the bubble above your head.
Normal text: send a message without any emoji code -> it shows exactly as in the normal game.
Graphics change: change the graphics settings and Apply, then relog -> no crash and emojis still show.
Palette search: open the palette, scroll with the wheel and the scrollbar, type 'cry' in its search box (game keys do nothing meanwhile), press Enter -> the first result goes into your message.
Animated emoji: in /say send text, a few emojis and an animated one from the Gif tab -> each shows in its place, the animated one moving; the bubble over your head shows them too.

Patron icons in chat: pick Patron I, then II, then III in the bubble choice window and write in /say -> the icon before your name is the same image as the one in the window (never a blue diamond for Patron III).
Chat badges: tick 'Class icon in chat', 'Level in chat' and 'Guild name in chat' (Settings > Features), write in /say -> your line starts with your class icon, level and [guild] in green.
Badges from far away: with the 3 badge options on, stand near a guild mate, then go to another map -> when he writes in Guild chat, his line still shows his class icon and level.
Peer search: tick 'Peer list search', open the Peer Chnl window (P) -> type part of a player name, or pick a class, a level or a channel -> only matching players stay; 'x' shows everyone again.

Peer channels: Peer Chnl window, channel filter -> every channel of the server is listed in order, even empty ones; press Update -> each shows its player count, e.g. 'Ch02 (0)'; pick one -> only its players.
Sounds panel: click the Sfx button next to the Emoji button -> the Sounds panel opens ('Click: chat input. Shift+click: preview.'); Shift+click a sound -> only you hear it.
Sounds in Party: you and a friend with the Eden client in a party -> send a sound in Party chat -> only party members hear it; a player next to you outside the party hears nothing.

Mute a chat for sounds: in the Sounds panel row (Say, Party, Guild, Peer, Couple, Whisper, World) click Party -> it greys out, a friend's party sound no longer plays (yours still does); relog -> kept.
One sound per line: with two chat tabs that both show Party (e.g. All and a Party tab) -> send one sound -> you hear it only once.
New sounds arrive: on a PC that never played before, wait 30 s in game and open the Sounds panel -> Tom Scream, Ive got this, Faah and Emotional Damage are listed.
Mute a player's sounds: right-click a player's name in the chat -> 'Mute sounds'; he sends a sound -> you see its icon and name but hear nothing; right-click him again -> 'Unmute sounds'.
Busy chat: stand in Aven with the chat open for 10 minutes while players duel nearby (many duel and combat lines) -> no crash, the chat keeps scrolling.
Time option: chat settings button > Channel Settings -> right of 'Buzz' are 'Time' and '12h'; tick 'Time', Confirm, write in /say -> new lines start with the time, e.g. [21:42], instead of <Say>.
Time on system lines: with 'Time' on, pick up gold or accept a quest -> the system line starts with the time too; lines already in the chat keep their old look.
Time with links: with 'Time' on, send one /say line with an emoji, an item link and a chat sound -> the emoji shows, link and name stay clickable, the sound plays, the time shows once at the start.
12h format: tick '12h' too and Confirm -> new lines show the time like [9:42 PM]; relog -> both boxes are still ticked.
Time and badges: 'Time' and 'Class icon in chat' both on -> a line reads time, class icon, level, [guild], then the name; a long message on two lines has the time only on its first line.
Bubble button: Channel Settings -> the last row has 'Bubble: Classic' with a small bubble icon; click it -> a 'Chat Bubble' window opens with 6 tiles: Classic, Ribbon, Flame, Frost, Leaf, Royal.

Others see your bubble: a player with the Eden client next to you sees your decorated bubble; a player without the Eden client sees the normal bubble and no strange chat line.
Every style: try Ribbon, Flame, Frost, Leaf and Royal with a short word, a long message on several lines and a message with emojis -> the frame fits, the text stays inside, emojis show.

/api/features/detail/class_codex/client?.name: class_codex

client.description: One window listing every class of the character's race, laid out like the admin's mockup: on the left each class on its own bar with the game's badge, its name, Lv x / max, an EXP bar with the EXP numbers and its state (Current class on a gold tag, Unlocked, Can unlock, padlock + Locked); click a class to see on the right its description from the game, How to unlock (each required level with yours in brackets, or the game's quest text) or Your progress, its Characteristics and Class Stat Bonus, and its awakening path. A 'Show locked classes' box (saved per PC) hides the classes not owned yet. Opens with the Codex button added to the title bar of the Class window, Alt+J, /codex in the chat or the shortcut bar; Escape, Close or the X closes it. Client only: everything is read from what the game already knows, nothing is sent to the server.
