# class_codex — CHANGELOG

## [0.7.2] - 2026-11-15 - Class Planner filled for the new races (planner 0.1.4)
- Planner : la fiche de classe etait acceptee seulement si son id valait `classe + 100 x (nibble >> 1)` (`class_codex_planner.c` `snap_class`), donc nom de classe, % de stats, passifs et sorts vides pour la tortue (5xx), le panda roux (10xx), le loup (9xx), le golem (8xx), l'ogresse / l'ogre (11xx) et le singe (12xx). Elle passe maintenant par `cx_rec_id_ok` (meme regle que le Codex). L'arbre de talents garde l'indice natif `(nibble >> 1) & 7` (talents de la base, comme le jeu).
- Test `client/tests/planner/test_planner_races.py` (lance par `run_planner_tests.py`) : table des races lue dans les sources des features de race (11 xid : 3, 5, 7, 10, 12-17, 33, lignees comprises), classes 1-61 acceptees pour chaque race et chaque sexe ; l'ancien test refusait exactement les 7 races ci-dessus.
- `class_codex_planner_ops.h` regenere (`gen_planner_ops.py`, 1275 sorts de classe : lignes Ogre / Singe ajoutees, sorts 56125 / 605xx des races mis a jour, opcodes 2146-2149) : `test_planner_data.py` le trouvait perime.

## [0.7.1] - 2026-11-13 - Ogre / Monkey class rows
- `cx_rec_id_ok` : lignes 1101-1161 (Ogre, nibbles 0 / 1) et 1201-1261 (Singe, nibble 1) acceptees (lignees, lignes servies par le crochet C11 de turtle_race pour le joueur local). `class_codex_planner_ops.h` a regenerer apres installation des donnees.

## [0.7.0] - 2026-11-05 - Golem, Bunny, Dragon classes
- `cx_rec_id_ok` : lignes 801-861 pour le nibble 10 (Golem, seul `id + 800`, jamais 5xx de la tortue) ; 601-661 (nibbles 12/13) et 701-761 (14/15) deja couvertes par `id + 100 * (race >> 1)`, verrouillees par le test. `class_codex_planner_ops.h` regenere (1151 sorts de classe avec les fiches livrees par golem_race, bunny_race, dragon_race).

## [0.6.0] - 2026-11-04 - Red Panda classes
- Lignes de classe du Red Panda 1001-1061 acceptees pour le nibble 3 (`cx_rec_id_ok`) ; `class_codex_planner_ops.h` regenere (965 sorts de classe).

## [0.5.0] - 2026-11-04 - Wolf classes
- Lignes de classe du Loup 9xx acceptees pour le nibble 7 (`cx_rec_id_ok`) ; `class_codex_planner_ops.h` regenere avec les fiches de classe livrees par wolf_race (903 sorts de classe).

## [0.4.5] - 2026-11-01 - Planner data with the Turtle class bonuses (turtle_race 0.4.0 / 0.5.0)
- `class_codex_planner_ops.h` was out of date: the admin's `game_unpacked` already holds the turtle_race 0.4.0 rows
  501-561 (class bonuses 64840-64899, Shell Inscription 64735), the header had none of them. `gen_planner_ops.py` now
  reads `game_unpacked` with the C_Class / C_Spell / c_enchant rows shipped by a feature that ships class rows taken
  over it (today turtle_race, `client/assets/data`; private `_` features never), as the client has them once
  installed: the header no longer changes when the admin installs or repacks, and it already has Shell Mimicry 64900
  of the Turtle Mimic row 520 (turtle_race 0.5.0, col. 42). Class spells 779 -> 841 (+64735, +60 bonuses, +64900);
  opcodes, certificates, sets, twins unchanged.

## [0.4.4] - 2026-11-01 - Turtle class rows 501-561 accepted (turtle_race 0.2.0)
- turtle_race 0.2.0 gives the Turtle (race nibble 5) its own class rows 501-561 through an inline hook on the C_Class
  getter `0xCE72E0` (C11, the vtable pointer stays native). The codex read the row and refused it, because its id is
  not `id + 100 * (race >> 1)` (201). `cx_rec_id_ok` (`class_codex_core.h`) now also accepts `id + 500` for race
  nibble 5; every other race is unchanged. The Planner keeps the Anura percentages for a Turtle (accepted limit of v2).
- Tests: `test_core.c` `test_rec_id` (3 checks).

## [0.4.3] - 2026-10-31 - Planner opens on the current class, no colour code in Characteristics (planner 0.1.3)
- Admin report: the Planner always showed Warrior instead of the current class (Engineer). `JobWnd_NA` +0x164 is set to
  1 (Warrior) when the window is created (0x8B7294) and to a flag bit at its init (0x8B87CF); it only holds a class once
  the player clicks a class in the list (0x8B7A6F). The planner now snapshots it when the Class window opens and uses it
  only after it changes while the window is open; until then the current class.
- Admin report: Characteristics showed `(colour='FFFFFFFF')Armor Specialization`. The native skill text starts with
  CEGUI markup; the tooltip cleaner turned its brackets into parentheses. Markup tags (`[name=...]`) are now removed,
  other brackets still become parentheses (`pl_tip_clean`, 7 cases in `test_planner_layout.py`).

## [0.4.2] - 2026-10-30 - Codex and Planner buttons stay visible after a click in the Class window (planner 0.1.2)
- Admin report: clicking in the Class window made the Codex and Planner buttons disappear. Both buttons are NonClient children
  of `Root/Job` drawn in the title bar band; a click raises the clicked native child (title bar, panels) to the front of its
  siblings, which then covered the buttons.
- Both buttons are now `AlwaysOnTop` among the `Root/Job` children, so no native sibling can be raised above them.
- `test_sites.py`: AlwaysOnTop allowed once in the button setup of each file (`btn_setup`, `btn_sync`), still refused everywhere else.

## [0.4.1] - 2026-10-30 - Planner no longer switched off by crash_guard (planner 0.1.1)
- Admin report: no Planner in game. The admin's log (DLL 0.735.0): `class_codex planner v0.1.0: off: site 0x0078A7E0 differs
  (other game build)`. The game_.exe bytes are the expected ones; crash_guard puts its UI event guard on `sub_78A7E0` (5-byte
  inline hook, `cg_install_ui_dispatch_guard`) before class_codex starts, so the exact compare failed and the whole part stayed off.
- `sig_ok` (`class_codex_read.h`): exact bytes, or a function prologue (`55 8B EC`) already hooked by another feature, checked by
  the shared `eden_head_match` (`utils/hook.h`, same rule as wndhook for this address: jump, then the native bytes). Data sites in
  the middle of a function stil

parts.title: Class planner (simulation)
parts.desc: Planner button left of Codex in the Class window: saved build, unsaved board points and a Simulate mode for talents, certificates (slots 1-9) and skill levels, drawn on the native talent board. Nothing is sent to the server; closing the Class window puts the saved build back.
parts.label: Class planner (simulation)

checklist.item: Codex button: open the game's Class window -> a 'Codex' button shows in its title bar, left of the close button, without hiding the title.
Open and close: click 'Codex' in the Class window -> the 'Class Codex' window opens in the middle of the screen. Click 'Codex' again (or Close) -> it closes.
Layout: open the Class Codex -> top line 'Character Lv N - Current: <class> Lv N - Unlocked: N of N classes', 'Show locked classes' at the right, class list left, details right, Close at the bottom.
Look: Class Codex -> dark panels, each class on its own bar; your class has a gold 'Current class' tag, the selected row a thin gold frame, locked classes a small padlock and 'Locked'.
Hotkey: in the world press Alt+J -> the Class Codex opens; press Alt+J again -> it closes. No Windows error sound.
Change the hotkey: Settings > Hotkeys > Eden Reforged, set 'Class Codex' to another key -> the new key opens the codex, Alt+J no longer does, and the codex footer shows the new key.
Chat command: type /codex in the chat -> the codex opens, no 'Command Error'. Type /codex again -> it closes.
Command options: type /codex open -> the codex opens (stays open if it already is); type /codex close -> it closes.
Readability: every text (top line, rows, 'How to unlock', 'Class Preview', 'Awakening Path', footer) reads well on its background; nothing is cut or overlaps. Long names like Arch-Elementalist fit.
Your class: open the codex -> your class is selected and scrolled into view; its level, EXP and bar match your EXP bar; the right panel shows 'Your progress' and 'Current class: EXP updates live.'
Live EXP: codex open, kill a few monsters -> the EXP of your current class goes up within a second, in its row and in 'Your progress'.
Another owned class: gain EXP, change to another class you own, open the codex -> the new class has the gold tag; the old one shows 'Unlocked' with the level and EXP it had when you left it.
Order: the list shows Warrior then its awakenings (marked *), Magician then its awakenings, and so on. Awakenings that do not exist in the game never show unless you own one.
Locked class: click a class you do not own -> the right panel shows its badge, name, 'Base class' or 'Awakening of <base>', its description and 'How to unlock' with 'Needs:' and one line per need.
Need colours: in 'How to unlock' of a locked class -> each need shows your value in brackets (e.g. 'Character Lv 25 (63)'), dark green when reached, dark red when missing.
Locked row: a class you do not own shows an empty bar and its first missing need in orange; when every level need is met the row says 'Ready to unlock' in green.

Awakening names: click Asura, Rakshasa, Blade Acrobat, Elegant Dancer and Mimic -> the line under the name is always whole (e.g. 'Awakening of Martial Artist'), no row ends with '...', levels read 'Lv'.
Row tooltip: hover a class row -> a tooltip on short lines with its name, state, 'Awakening of <base>' for an awakening, what it needs and how to unlock it.
Other tooltips: hover the description -> the full description and the class knowledge text. Hover 'Class Preview' -> what the Class Stat Bonus means.
Show locked classes: untick it -> only your own classes stay and your selected class stays selected. Tick it -> the locked classes come back.
Setting kept: untick 'Show locked classes', close the game completely, start it again, open the codex -> the box is still unticked. Tick it again.
Level cap: a class at Lv 90 shows 'Lv 90 / 90', a full bar and 'Max level reached' in gold; 'Your progress' says 'Level 90 of 90'. Never 'Lv 90 / 100' nor EXP towards Lv 91.
Above the cap: on a GM character with a class at Lv 100 -> its row shows 'Lv 100' (never 'Lv 100 / 90'), a full bar and 'Max level reached'; 'Your progress' shows 'Level 100' only.
Class Preview: right panel, lower half -> 'Characteristics: <name>' (e.g. Bravery for Warrior) and 'Class Stat Bonus:' with HP, MP, STR, AGI, INT, WIS, LCK from strongest to weakest.
Stat numbers: compare 'Class Stat Bonus' in the codex with the game's Class window for the same class -> same numbers; green above 100, white at 100, orange below 100.
Awakening Path: right panel -> the base class and its awakenings with their level or state, the selected one framed in gold; a class without awakening says 'No awakening for this class yet.'
Escape: codex open, press Escape -> the codex closes and the game menu does NOT open.
Help first: open the '?' help of the codex, press Escape -> the help closes, the codex stays; press Escape again -> the codex closes.
Screen sizes: at 1280x720 and at 2560x1440 the codex fits on screen and reads well; drag it by its title bar to move it.
Scrolling: the class list scrolls with the mouse wheel; with many classes nothing overlaps.
Settings off: Settings > Features, untick 'Class Codex' -> the codex window and the Codex button disappear at once, Alt+J does nothing.
Settings on: tick 'Class Codex' again -> the Codex button comes back within a second and Alt+J opens the codex again, no restart needed.
Channel and teleport: change channel, then teleport, opening the codex each time -> it shows your classes, no error box, no crash.
Other character: go to the character list and log in with another character, open the codex -> it shows that character's classes, never the previous one's.
Open while leaving: codex open, go back to character select -> the codex closes with the world. Log in, open it -> every class icon shows, no empty square, no crash. Do it twice.

Shortcut bar: under the minimap hover the 'Codex' icon (blue open book) -> tooltip 'Codex (Alt+J)' (or your key), then 'Class Codex: every class of your race with its level, EXP and how to unlock it'.
Shortcut click: click the Codex icon under the minimap -> the Class Codex opens and the icon stays pressed; click again -> it closes and the icon is released.
Many classes: on a character with many classes, open the codex for the first time this session -> it shows at once, the rest of the list fills within a fraction of a second, no visible freeze.
Close buttons: close with the X, reopen, close with Close, reopen; go to character select and back and do it again -> each one closes the codex every time.
Adjudicator: click Adjudicator -> its description reads '... the power to pardon - or punish - all life on earth ...' (never 'No description in the game data.').
Long descriptions: click Berserker, Dragon Knight, Mimic, Inquisitor -> the whole text can be read with a scroll bar when long; it starts at the top for each class and never ends with '...'.
Short description: click Knight -> no scroll bar next to its description.
Escape order: open the Loot Tracker (Alt+L), then the codex (Alt+J), press Escape -> the codex closes first, the Loot Tracker at the second Escape.
Help after reopening: close and reopen the codex 5 times -> its '?' help still opens each time.
Planner button: open the Class window -> a 'Planner' button shows left of the 'Codex' button.
Planner panel: click 'Planner' -> a 'Class Planner' panel opens at the right of the Class window with 'Your saved build'; tabs Overview, Skills, Talents, Certificates show your numbers, nothing cut.
Board points: on the Class Talent board place 1 point without Confirm -> the planner reads 'Board: 1 KP placed, not saved yet' and Overview gets a 'Board' column.

Back to saved: after placing a point without Confirm, close and reopen the Class window -> the board is back to your saved build and the chat says 'Class Planner: 1 KP on the Class Talent board was not saved; ...'.
Nothing sent: after the previous test, relog -> your talent points are exactly as before (the point you never confirmed is not there).
Simulate: tick 'Simulate', then 'Plan to Lv 90' -> 'SIMULATION - not saved'; click, right-click and Shift + click board cells -> the cells show the planned levels and 'Plan: N KPs left'.
Simulation plate: while simulating, press and release on the 'Simulation' plate over Confirm -> nothing happens, Confirm is not pressed. Relog: your talents are unchanged.
Simulate off and on: untick 'Simulate' -> the plan leaves the board and it looks normal; tick it again -> the plan comes back unchanged.

Talents tab: click Clear -> tree at 0. Shift + click a node -> it goes to the max your points allow. Right-click a needed node below its level -> the nodes that need it drop to 0 with a 'set to 0' note.
Talent refusals: raise a node above what its needed node allows, or past your points -> red text 'Needs ...' or 'Not enough KPs: ...' and nothing changes.
Certificates tab: click a certificate in the list, then slot 3 -> the old one goes back to the list, tier II replaces tier I, combos update. Right-click a slot -> it is emptied in the plan.
Skills tab: click + on a skill -> 'Lv a > b' with MP and Power at the new level; hover its icon -> 'Simulated: Lv b (yours: Lv a)' then the game's text.
Stat tooltip: in the Class window hover a Class Stat Bonus number -> e.g. 'Class base at Lv 90: 117 x 135% = 158' then '(before talents, certificates, equipment and buffs)'.
Other class: pick another class in the list of the Class window -> the planner panel follows it and its header says '(not current)'.
End of simulation: with a plan on, change map (or go to character select and back), reopen the Class window -> no crash; chat 'Class Planner: simulation ended, your saved build is back.'
Normal Confirm: with Simulate unticked, place 1 point, press Confirm, close the window at once -> the point is saved (still there after relog), no 'not saved' message.

Planner option: Class window open, untick 'Class planner (simulation)' under Class Codex in Settings > Features -> the Planner button and panel go; tick it -> the button is back, the panel stays closed.
Whole feature off: with the planner open, untick 'Class Codex' -> the Codex and Planner buttons and the panel go; tick it again -> the buttons come back.
Small screens: at 1280x720 the panel sits right of the Class window; at 1024x768 it is a folded band at the right edge with '+' that unfolds over the board. Nothing cut.
Escape with the planner: panel open, press Escape -> the help or the panel closes first; Escape again -> the Class window closes.
Planner slots 8 and 9: Certificates tab -> 9 slots; slots 8 and 9 show your real certificates marked as half value; closing the Class window never changes your real slots.
Death: die with the Class Codex open, then revive -> no crash; close it, type /codex -> it opens on your class with the same level and EXP.
Off and chat: untick 'Class Codex' in Settings > Features, type /codex in the chat -> no Class Codex window opens.
Off after restart: untick 'Class Codex', close the game completely, start it again -> no 'Codex' button in the Class window until you tick it again.
Level up live: codex open, gain a level on your current class -> its row and 'Your progress' show the new level within a second.
Party: in a party, open the codex -> it lists only your own classes and levels, never those of a party member.

# class_shortcuts — Changelog

## [0.1.0] — 2026-10-19 — FIX: skill bars stuck on the previous class (player report)
- **Bug (players, "old X-Legend bug"):** after a class change the shortcut bars could keep the skills of another
  class, for days, and every later class change spread them. Cause, read in the three binaries: the MissionServer
  keeps one set of bars per class plus the shown bars, and switches them only when the client, after its class
  packet, sends the class it left (`TC_UpdateClassShortcut`). A client that never sends it (crash or disconnection
  right after the change) or two changes faster than that round trip leave the bars of one class under another;
  the MissionServer keeps that in memory until it restarts and writes it to the database at the next edit.
- **Fix (MissionServer, in-memory patch):** `TC_UpdateClass` switches the bars itself with the class it replaces
  and sends them to the client; the class sent by the client is no longer used as a key (its request only resends
  the bars). No client change, no database change.
- Tests: native MissionServer code emulated (bug reproduced natively in 3 scenarios, fixed with the patch, edge
  cases) 25/25; `mempatch_check` 0 error.
- GM procedure and SQL (read-only diagnosis, repair with backup, restore): `server/sql/`, study §5.

checklist.item: Use a character with two unlocked classes (e.g. Warrior and Ranger). Put skills on the 1-0 and F1-F10 bars, change class in the Class window, set other skills. Change back and forth: each class gets its own skills back.
Change class in the Class window and close the game at once (Alt+F4), before the bars change. Log back in: the bars show the skills of your NEW class. Change back: the old class has its own skills.
Change class several times quickly (Warrior, Ranger, Knight, Warrior...). After each change the bars show the skills of the class you are now. Relog: same bars.
Items, mounts and bar pages (small arrows) follow the class too. Relog or change zone without changing class: nothing on the bars moves.
Logout right after a change: change class in the Class window, then go to character select at once -> log in again: the bars show your new class's skills; change back: the old class has its own.
New skill stays on its class: change class, drag a new skill onto F3, relog, change back to the old class -> the old class's F3 is unchanged; the new skill is only on the new class.
Three classes: put a different skill on slot 1 for three classes (e.g. Warrior, Ranger, Knight), switch through all three twice -> slot 1 always shows the skill of the class you are on.
Channel change right after a class change: change class, then change channel at once -> on arrival the bars show the new class's skills; change back: the old class's skills.
Other character: change class on character A, then log in with character B of the same account -> B's bars are B's own, never A's skills.
Class never played: change to a class you unlocked but never used -> its bars are its own (empty or default), never filled with the skills of the class you just left.
Keys fire the right skill: after several class changes press each bar key (1-0, F1-F10) -> each one fires the skill shown on its slot, never a skill of another class.
Full restart: set different bars on two classes, close the game completely, start it again and switch between the two classes -> each class shows its own bars.
Zone change after a class change: change class, then teleport to another zone at once -> on arrival the bars show the new class's skills.
Death after a class change: change class, die and revive -> the bars still show the new class's skills.
Party: in a party, change class -> your bars switch to the new class; a party member's bars never change.

# collect_all — CHANGELOG

## v0.8.0 — 2026-11-12 (client only, MissionServer patch 0.5.1 unchanged)
- Tester request "add receive all icon on top of window": the commissions window (`Root/Work`, `WorkListWnd.layout`,
  title row "Amount of Commissions: N/10") gets a native `DejaVu/Button` **Receive all** at the top right, on the count
  row (`Root/Work/Static/EdenReceiveAllBtn`, x 190-264 y 7-32 of the 276 x 268 client area, right edge on the list
  frame, 9 px after the end of "Amount of Commissions: 10/10", 10 px above the list frame). No asset, no repack.
- One click = every finished commission, one at a time, with the native request of the row's Receive/OK
  (`0x6CE1E0(slot)`, the same call the game makes itself for auto-received commissions in `0x711D90`): finished =
  table entry `+0x30 == 1` (set by the "work finished" packet `0x711ECB`, read by the menu notification `0x891EA3`);
  the next one 350 ms after the answer (`0x70FFF0` clears the entry, `+0x30 = -1` in `0x776FD0`). Running
  commissions are never sent. Stops on bag full (text 1273, ZoneServer `CWorkManager::WorkResultOK` `0x8164C12`),
  3 s without answer, window closed, zone change, Game Reset, feature off, or a second click (Stop). One chat line
  "Receive all: N commission(s) received." Native per-row Receive untouched (no hook in the window).
- Four code sites checked at init (`0x6CE1E0`, `0x71001C`, `0x711ECB`, `0x776FF2`); any mismatch = no button.
- Host tests: `test_claim` +11 scenarios (229 checks), new `test_work_layout.py` (32 checks, scales 1.0/1.2/1.5).

## v0.7.0 — 2026-10-30 (client only, MissionServer patch 0.5.1 unchanged)
- Tester feedback "this is not deleting empty mails": the delete option only deleted the mails emptied by the same
  click. A mail already empty when the run started (collected earlier with the native button, or by a run with the
  box unticked) was skipped by the list reader (`read_page`, "no item and no gold" = not tracked) and by the ticked
  rows reader (`sel_rows`), so "Collect all & del" deleted nothing in a box of old empty mails, and 35 of them in front
  stopped the run with "delete some letters to reach the others".
- The option is now "Delete empty mails": with it ticked, every mail that holds nothing, has been read and is not cash on
  delivery is deleted too (read flag = list packet `vector<u16>` at `pkt+0x158`, row byte `+0x50`, filled by
  `0xAB2150`). Unread letters (never opened, nothing attached) are kept; the MissionServer marks a mail read when an
  attachment is taken (`GetMailItem`/`GetMailGold` set `mail+0x35` = `opened`), so every mail collected earlier
  qualifies. Ticked mails: the ticked read empty ones are deleted as well, and a click on empty mails only sends no
  collect batch. Tooltips and the "unread letters" reason updated.
- Host tests: `test_claim` +6 scenarios (old empty mails with delete, only old empty mails, delete unticked, 35 read empty
  mails in front of 10 gold mails, ticked mails with a read empty one, ticked empty mails only); 194 checks pass.

- Asset/site fallback audit: when the altar Claim code `0x6CDBE0` is not the expected one (other game build, or a
  foreign detour), the altar part was logged off but the bar was still changed: the native Claim button was raised and
  an empty "Claim all" button (no text, click without effect) was added under it. The bar is now left native in that
  case (the `[feature_init] collect_all: unexpected code at 0x006CDBE0, altar bar Claim all off` line is the only trace);
  mail and login rewards parts unchanged.
- Audit (no change): S1 prod CDN pkg / S2 pristine pkg - no asset of ours, every widget is created by the DLL under native
  parents; S3 - the 8 hook prologues are checked byte for byte before anything is written (feature off otherwise);
  S4 - MissionServer without the paging patch: page 6 probed once per session, 35-mail limit kept with a chat hint.
- Tests: `test_claim.c` scenario "altar unknown game code: bar left native" (+3 checks). All scenarios pass.

## v0.6.7 — 2026-10-22 (client only)
- Tester feedback "tooltip can't read all": a CEGUI tooltip does not wrap, so a line longer than about 52 characters runs off the screen. The mail and altar tooltips are now cut into lines of at most 52
  columns: "Claim every reached reward of this bar, one after the other", the two "...then delete the mails this
  click emptied" texts and the delete check box text (115 characters on one line before).
- Tests: `test_claim.c` checks every collect_all tooltip line (9 texts) fits 52 columns. All scenarios pass.

- **Turning collect_all off gives the altar bar and the login rewards panel their native layout back.** The native

0.8.0 Receive all: have 2 or more commissions showing '0 min. 0 sec. remaining.' and 1 still running -> click 'Receive all' -> every finished one is received one after the other (button shows 'Stop (n)'), the running one stays in the list; chat 'Receive all: N commission(s) received.' with N = the finished ones; the items are in your bag.
0.8.0 Nothing finished: every commission still running -> 'Receive all' is greyed, tooltip 'No commission is finished yet'; it turns active by itself when one reaches 0 sec.
0.8.0 Bag full: 3 finished commissions and almost no free bag slot -> 'Receive all' -> what fits is received, the chat line ends with '(bag full)', the rest stays in the list (nothing lost).
0.8.0 Native Receive still works: click the 'Receive' button of one finished row -> the native result window opens as before and its Receive gives the reward; 'Receive all' then skips that one.

0.8.0 Stop and close: click 'Receive all' with 4+ finished, click it again at once -> it stops ('(stopped)'); start again and close the window during the run -> it stops ('(the window was closed)'), nothing more is received until you click again.

0.7.0 Old empty mails: have 3 or more mails you already collected earlier (open, nothing attached) and 1 mail with gold -> tick 'Mark All' and 'Delete empty mails', click 'Collect all & del' -> the gold is taken and ALL the empty mails vanish; chat 'Collect all: 1 attachment(s) collected, N mail(s) deleted.'

0.7.0 Nothing to collect: a mailbox with only empty read mails -> 'Mark All' + 'Delete empty mails' -> 'Collect all & del' -> they are all deleted ('0 attachment(s) collected, N mail(s) deleted.'). An unread letter (never opened) stays.

0.7.0 Ticked empty mails: 'Mark All' unticked, 'Delete empty mails' ticked -> tick only 2 empty read mails, click 'Collect & delete' -> both vanish, chat 'Collect: 0 attachment(s) collected, 2 mail(s) deleted.'
Collect all mail tooltip: open a mailbox, tick 'Mark All' -> hover the bottom 'Collect all mail' button -> the tooltip reads 'Collect the attachments of every page'.

Claim all, bag full: Activities > Everyday with several login rewards ready and only ONE free bag slot -> click 'Claim all (N)' -> what fits is claimed, one chat line ends with '(bag full)', nothing is lost.

Claim all at once: free 8 or more bag slots, Activities > Everyday -> one click on 'Claim all (N)' -> every ready reward is claimed at once (the button may flash 'Stop n/N') and the reward lines come together.
Claim all counts: note the login rewards that are ready, click 'Claim all (N)' -> check your bag -> each ready day gave exactly its reward: no day claimed twice, none missing.
Claimed for good: after Claim all, log out and back in, open Activities > Everyday -> the claimed days stay claimed and 'Claim all' is greyed with the tooltip 'Nothing to claim yet'.

Claim all stop: click 'Claim all (N)' and click it again at once while it shows 'Stop n/N' -> it stops and the chat says 'Claim all: n of N reward(s) claimed (stopped).' (it is fast, try a few times).
Claim all chat line: claim several login rewards with 'Claim all (N)' -> one chat line 'Claim all: N reward(s) claimed.', with N matching the rewards received.
Mail window layout: open a mailbox -> top row: 'Mark All', then the 'Delete empty mails' checkbox (unticked), then help. Bottom row: Collect All, Delete, Close. No extra button at the top.
Native Collect All: 'Mark All' and 'Delete empty mails' unticked -> the bottom button reads 'Collect All'; tick 1 or 2 mails and click it -> only those mails are taken, like the normal game.
Mark All label: 'Delete empty mails' unticked -> tick 'Mark All' -> the button turns 'Collect all mail' at once; untick it -> back to 'Collect All'.
Labels with Delete: tick 'Mark All' and 'Delete empty mails' -> 'Collect all & del'; untick 'Mark All' -> 'Collect & delete'; untick Delete -> 'Collect All'. Each change is instant.
Labels after reopening: close and reopen the mailbox (also after a zone change) -> the button label matches the checkboxes; the 'Delete empty mails' tick is remembered until you log out.

Collect all mail: 3 to 5 pages of mails with items and gold, tick 'Mark All' -> click 'Collect all mail' -> the list does not flip pages, the button counts ('Stop 12/35'), chat 'Collect all: N attachment(s) collected.'
After the run: when 'Collect all mail' ends -> the page you were on reloads once and shows the emptied mails; 'Mark All' unticks itself and the label goes back to 'Collect All'.

Collect all & del: tick 'Mark All' and 'Delete empty mails' -> click 'Collect all & del' -> 'Stop del 5/20' after the collect, the emptied mails vanish, one chat line '... collected, M mail(s) deleted.'
Counts are right: after a run -> N in the chat matches what arrived in your bag and gold, M matches the mails that vanished. No mail taken twice, no duplicated item, no error spam.

Ticked mails only: 'Mark All' unticked, 'Delete empty mails' ticked -> tick 2 mails with items and 1 empty read mail, click 'Collect & delete' -> the 2 are taken then deleted, the empty read one is deleted too.
Cash on delivery is safe: have a cash-on-delivery mail and run 'Collect all & del' -> that mail is never paid, taken or deleted; an unread letter (never opened, nothing attached) also stays.

Bag almost full: 2 free bag slots and 7 or more item mails -> 'Collect all mail' -> 2 items taken, gold mails still taken, chat ends with 'bag full, some items are still in the mailbox'. Nothing lost.
Gold at maximum: gold close to 999,999,999 and a gold mail that would go over -> 'Collect all mail' -> that gold stays in the mailbox, items are taken, chat says 'gold at maximum...'. No gold lost.
Stop button: click the button while it shows 'Stop ...' -> it stops at once, the chat gives the exact count so far, the page reloads once; nothing else is taken or deleted.
Interrupted run: close the mailbox, switch to the Send tab or change zone during a run -> it stops, the mailbox does not reopen by itself and the game stays stable.
Scroll during a run: during a run scroll the list or untick 'Mark All' -> the run goes on and the button stays clickable (Stop); at the end the list shows the page the scrollbar points to.
Trade lock: on a character with trading locked -> run 'Collect all mail' -> it stops with 'trade is locked on this character', nothing is taken and nothing is deleted.
Auction mails: sell, buy and cancel a sale at the auction house -> 'Collect all mail' picks up those auction mails (item or gold) like any other mail.
Fast clicks: click the button 10 times quickly -> it only starts and stops, one run at a time, never a doubled item or doubled gold.
Two players at once: two characters run 'Collect all & del' at the same time on big mailboxes -> no lag for other players, each gets exactly his own mail.
After a relog: log out and back in, reopen the mailbox and Activities > Everyday -> labels and buttons work, no crash.
Big mailbox: 50 or more mails with items or gold -> tick 'Mark All' and 'Delete empty mails', click 'Collect all & del' -> the button counts like 'Stop 12/35' and the mailbox empties completely.
Past page 5: 50 or more mails with items -> tick only 'Mark All' and click 'Collect all mail' -> mails past the 35th are collected too, without changing zone.
Reading every page: 50 or more mails -> scroll the mailbox list to its end -> pages past page 5 show without changing zone.
Delete tooltip: hover 'Delete empty mails' -> it explains that every empty mail you have read is deleted, never cash on delivery, never an unread letter, never a mail that still holds something.
Claim all nothing ready: Activities > Everyday with no reward ready -> 'Claim all' is greyed and its tooltip reads 'Nothing to claim yet'.
Claim all with free slots again: after a '(bag full)' stop -> free some bag slots and click 'Claim all (N)' again -> the rest is claimed.
Claim all window closed: during a Claim all close the Activities window -> it stops and the chat line ends with '(window closed)'; nothing is lost.
Altar Claim all: Crafting Altar, Crystal or Star Diamond tab, progress bar past 3 steps -> click 'Claim all' under 'Claim' -> the rewards arrive one by one, then the button turns grey.
Altar chat line: after an altar Claim all -> chat 'Claim all: N reward(s) of the bar claimed.' with N matching the rewards received.
Altar layout: open the Crafting Altar progress bar -> 'Claim' and 'Claim all' are stacked in the same column, nothing overlaps or is cut.
Altar nothing ready: a progress bar with no step reached -> 'Claim all' is greyed and its tooltip reads 'No reward of this bar is ready'.
Altar Stop: click 'Claim all' and click again while it reads 'Stop (N)' -> it stops; the rewards already claimed are in the bag.
Altar bag full: altar Claim all with a full bag -> it stops with '(bag full)' in the chat, nothing lost.
Altar closed: close the altar during a Claim all -> it stops ('the altar was closed').
Collect All off: untick 'Collect All' in Settings > Features -> the mailbox, Everyday and altar work like the normal game at once; tick it -> 'Claim all' and 'Collect all mail' are back.
Off during a run: during a mail run untick 'Collect All' -> the run stops and the button reads 'Collect All' again.
Claim all tooltip: Activities > Everyday with a reward ready -> hover 'Claim all (N)' -> the tooltip reads 'Claim every reward that is ready, all at once'.
Altar Claim all tooltip: Crafting Altar with 2 or more steps reached -> hover 'Claim all' -> the tooltip reads 'Claim every reached reward of this bar, one after the other'.
Stop tooltip: during a 'Collect all mail' run -> hover the button while it reads 'Stop ...' -> the tooltip reads 'Click to stop'.
Off from the start: start the game with 'Collect All' unticked in Settings > Features -> the mailbox has only the normal Collect All button, no 'Delete empty mails', and Everyday has no 'Claim all'.
Bag full and gold at maximum: full bag, gold near 999,999,999, item and gold mails -> 'Collect all mail' -> chat ends with 'bag full and gold at maximum'; those items and gold stay in the mailbox.
More mails waiting: a run ends with 'more mails are waiting: click again' -> click the button again -> the next mails are collected; nothing is taken twice.
Hidden mails: a run ends with 'the server lists only the first N mails...' -> tick 'Delete empty mails' and click again -> the mails after them are collected too.

/api/features/detail/confirm_actions/cli.name: confirm_actions

client.description: Asks before three one-click actions that cannot be taken back, in the game's own Yes / No box: Revive in the death window (back to your Soul Guardian) asks 'Revive at your Soul Guardian now?', the 'Teleport me to Aven' choice of the Guild benefits board asks 'Teleport to Aven now?', and Reset UI in the main menu (Esc) asks 'Reset the interface? Every window goes back to its default place. This cannot be undone.'. Yes does exactly what the button did before, No or Escape cancels. Each part can be switched off on its own in Settings > Features. The box closes by itself when the game moves on (revived by the countdown, another player or an arena / dungeon timer, board closed, character change), so a forced revive or teleport is never held back; Revive Here, Revival Item, Accept / Refuse Revive and every other button are untouched. Client DLL only, nothing to repack, nothing on the server. The Treasure Archive's Archive All confirmation lives in the archive feature.

/api/features/detail/confirm_actions/cli.changelog:
# confirm_actions — CHANGELOG

## v0.1.3 (2026-10-26) — hooks only on the expected game code (asset/site audit)
- S3 (other game build): the Revive and NPC option click hooks checked only the stolen bytes, a generic prologue
  (`55 8B EC 64 A1 00000000`, `55 8B EC 83 EC 10`) that thousands of functions share. Another function at that
  address would have been hooked and called back with our argument count (stack imbalance). Both now check 16 bytes
  that identify the function (SEH handler `0xE5A203` for Revive, list box offset `+0xE0` and the call that follows
  for the NPC board); still 9 / 6 bytes stolen. On a mismatch nothing is written and the existing
  `[feature_init] confirm_actions ... NOT hooked` line says which part stays native. Reset UI already checked its
  call target. No asset, no server part.

## v0.1.2 (2026-10-19) — Escape only closes the box; Revive box closes when the Revive button goes away
Preprod tests (marlowmoss, SantaKurai, 0.1.1 / EDEN 0.471.0 on the preprod branch, votes 2026-10-19).
- **Escape also closed the guild board / the main menu (#8, #12)**. The game does not read Escape from window
  messages: `sub_6A8250` reads the **DirectInput** keyboard (`[0x1057338]`, Esc = bit 2 of `+0x21` now and not of
  `+0x41` before, `0x6A82B0`) and then closes every open window (`sub_78A460` -> `sub_7955B0`: NPC board, main menu,
  bag...) or opens the main menu. 0.1.0 / 0.1.1 only ate `WM_KEYDOWN` and the `GetAsyncKeyState` / `GetKeyState`
  imports, which this path never uses: our box closed, and the game closed everything else on the same press.
  Fix (`utils/confirm.c`, EDEN 0.461.0, also used by the archive's Archive All): the 5 bytes `mov eax,[0x1057338]` at
  `0x6A82B0` jump to a stub; on an Escape press with one of our boxes open it answers No (message 1002, as before)
  and skips the game's Escape branch (`0x6A838D`, next key); a press within 0.5 s of a box closed by Escape is
  skipped too (the window-message path and the DirectInput path see the same press in either order). Without a box,
  Escape is untouched (the stub returns to `0x6A82B5`). Bytes checked before patching (opcode, `[0x1057338]`, the
  `test byte [eax+0x21],2` that follows); unknown build = no hook, logged.
- **Revive box left open after a friend's revive offer (#6)**. The death window does not hide when a player offers a
  revive: message 121 (`sub_80FB80`) hides Revive / Revive Here / Revival Item and shows Accept / Refuse. 0.1.1 only
  watched the window, so the box stayed ("Revive at your Soul Guardian now?" above Accept / Refuse) and its Yes still
  sent the Soul Guardian revive. The box now follows the **Revive button itself** (the clicked `DirectBtn`, its own
  visible flag `+0xB8`): it closes by itself as soon as the button is hidden or the window closes, and Yes re-checks
  it.
- **"No countdown" after No (#2) is the game's normal death window**: the countdown (`CountDownText` `+0xF8`, texts
  350 "Time: %s1" / 7578 "Time until revival: %s1 seconds") and the Revive button are never shown together
  (`sub_80FDB0` shows the buttons and hides the countdown; every countdown hides the buttons until it ends). The box
  never touches the death window (No = nothing). The test steps that asked for a countdown next to Revive were wrong
  and are rewritten.
- Tests: state bench 123/123 (new: game Escape path through the real stub - no box = native, box = No + skipped,
  held key, 0.5 s grace, window-message Escape first then DirectInput, outside the world, unknown site bytes; Revive:
  No leaves window and button alone, revive offer closes the box, Yes after the button went away sends nothing);
  sites 166 checks (Escape site / skip target / native close-all and main-menu calls, DirectBtn hidden by the revive
  offer and the countdowns, CEGUI own flag `+0xB8`).

## v0.1.1 (2026-10-17) — Teleport me to Aven: Yes always teleports
- **Bug (player report)**: after "Teleport to Aven now?" the Yes button often did nothing; it worked on the 4th try.
  Cause: the board's option list is a `DejaVu/Listbox2`, mapped to **`CEGUI/ComboDropList`** (`DejaVu.scheme`). Once
  clicked, that list is "armed" (`+0x3D5`, set by `onMouseButtonDown` `0xBE2000`) and its `onMouseMove`
  (`0xBE1F70`) moves the selection to the row under the mouse (`setItemSelectState` `0xBE1560`) or clears it over an
  empty part of the list (`clearAllSelections` `0xBE0110`). Going from "Teleport me to Aven" to the box's Yes button
  the mouse usually crosses "Check guild goods" / "Open Auction House" or the empty space under them, so at Yes the
  selected row was no longer the Aven one; 0.1.0 re-read the selection, saw another row and sent nothing ("the board
  no longer shows that choice"). It only worked when the mouse left the list straight from the Aven row.
- Fix: Yes no longer reads the list selection. The option index and value are kept when the box opens; Yes checks
  that the board is still open and still offers that value at that index (`+0x10C` vector), then does exactly what
  the native click `0x8176A0` does for that index: index kept at `+0x100`, `sub_6CC550(index)` (same packet),
  `+0x148` / `+0x140` cleared. Hovering other rows while the box is open changes nothing.
- Shared box (`utils/confirm.c`, EDEN 0.432.0, also used by the archive's Archive All): the box is now tied to the
  zone it was opened in (`eden_world_epoch`): a zone change / teleport while it is open closes it, and a Yes after a
  zone change does nothing (an in-game teleport keeps the game state at 8, so the old "in the world" test did not see
  it).
- Tests: new `client/tests/run_tests.py` (run by `ops_test_feature`): `state/test_state.c` builds the real
  `confirm_actions.c` + `utils/confirm.c` against a mocked game (box, board, list, revive window, zone, Game Reset)
  and checks 87 cases (Yes after hover moved / cleared the selection, page changed, board closed, zone change, Game
  Reset, double click on the option, double Yes, No, Escape, parts / feature o

/api/features/detail/costume_dye/client?.name: costume_dye

client.description: The costume dye window gets a docked 'Dye parts' window: up to 7 parts per costume (parts 1-3 = main colours, part 4 on 12 costumes, parts 5-7 = the biggest separate pieces of the costume dye mask; 6 or 7 parts on most costumes), every costume dye of your bag for this costume type with how many you have, click a part then a dye to see it on the 3D model (nothing is used), Reset, and Apply which lists exactly the dyes that will be used before dyeing. The server stays the judge: each part is one native dye use (item checked, consumed, colour saved and shown to every player); it stops at the first refused part. The colour stays one 64-bit item value (7 palette indexes once a piece is dyed), rendered by the DLL with a baked mask texture per item. Server (in-memory patch only, ZoneServer): dye zones 1-11 on costumes. Server data: 2948 costumes that have a dye mask become dyeable (S_Item / S_ItemMall column 11 bit 28, revert clears it). Costumes without any dye area are refused before a dye is used.

# crash_guard — CHANGELOG
## [1.24.0 / core 0.32.0] — 2026-11-04 (x87 exceptions unmasked near 4 GB)

- **x87 guard (VEH, `crash_guard_fpu.h`)**: 22 prod reports since 28/10 (20 installs, DLL 0.658 and 0.733) died on an
  x87 FPU exception in game_.exe: `0xC000008F` `+0x1C1228` `sub_5C11F0+0x38` (12, inexact result on the `fldcw
  [ebp-2]` that follows `fistp`), `0xC000008E` `+0x684A5` (4, divide by zero), `0xC0000090` `+0x52845` (3, invalid),
  `+0x60FFB`, `+0x19E783`, `+0x1C4850`. All 22 at 4011-4076 MB of virtual memory: when the address space is nearly
  full, the main thread's x87 control word loses its exception masks (the game is built for the Windows default, all
  masked; no code of game_.exe unmasks on purpose: the 4 `_controlfp` calls belong to the static HLSL compiler and
  mask everything). Who clears them is not proven (lead: HLSL compiler destructor `sub_60DC69` restores
  `[obj+0x2A0]` with mask `0xB001F`, a zero there gives exactly "all unmasked, 64-bit precision").
- On `0xC000008D..0xC0000093` with EIP in game_.exe `.text`, a pending flag that is unmasked in the context and no
  game `__try` owning it: exception masks set back (`FCW |= 0x3F` in FXSAVE and FloatSave), flags cleared (`FSW &=
  0x7F00`, TOP and C0-C3 kept), and when the waiting instruction is `fldcw m16` the saved word it reloads is fixed
  too (otherwise the function puts the unmasked word back and traps again). Execution continues at the same
  instruction. An inexact result is already stored when it traps, so the continued run gives the same values as the
  masked run (proven); for divide by zero / invalid the destination keeps the unmasked response, once (the next
  ones are masked). Nothing changes while the masks are correct (the handler sees no pending unmasked flag and
  passes). 256 per 2 s at most, then the crash as before.
- error.log: `[crash_guard] native-guard x87 install=1 (...)` at start, `[crash_guard] RECOVERED x87 exception
  code=... EIP=game_.exe+0x... cw=0x.... sw=0x.... -> FPU exceptions masked again ...` (8 then 1/1024); the `cw`
  value is the clue for the culprit. Guard counter `fpu_mask`.
- Tests: `tests/test_fpu_mask_v032.c` 26/26 (real traps on the host: copy of the bytes of `sub_5C11F0` with the
  real constant `0xBB7E01FC`, unmasked = 1 trap, same result as masked, saved word fixed, 10000 later calls without
  trap, convergence after a new unmask, divide by zero once then inf; `fldcw` decoder: `[ebp+d8]`, `[abs32]`,
  `[esp+d8]`, `[ecx]`, `[ebp+d32]`, SIB; the instructions of the sites `0x4684A5` / `0x452845` are not `fldcw`).
- Study: `docs/studies/crashes_2026-11-04.md` (other signatures of 28/10-04/11: visual_effects 1.9.2 family and
  trade + loot_roll_pos family, already gone on 0.733; NiStream / OOM families, no safe guard).


## [1.23.0 / reporter 0.8.0 + utils perf] — 2026-10-30 (freeze diagnostics)

- **Short freeze sample (reporter 0.8.0)**: the hang watch only reported a freeze after 30 s (`CR_HANG_S`), so the
  3-10 s freezes players describe after a kill left nothing. The watchdog thread now takes ONE sample of the main
  thread when it has been silent for 3 s (`CR_STALL_S`, in game only, at most 3 per session, `CR_STALL_MAX`): the
  same `crcore_capture_thread` as the hang capture (suspension of a few microseconds, no dump, nothing done on the
  game or render thread), then one line `[crashrep] short freeze n/3: main thread silent 3 s, map M (sample,
  suspended N us): EIP <module+off | game_.exe VA> | game_.exe caller 0x... | eden owner eden.dll+0x... | frames
  ...` (6 EBP frames). Module names come from `GetMappedFileName` (no loader lock); the module ranges are read once
  when the watchdog starts (`crcore_stall_prime`). The 30 s hang report is unchanged.
- **utils/perf.c: EIP of THAT frame on a hitch of 1 s or more**: the sampler (every ~4 ms) also fills small per-frame
  bins (game_.exe EIP, eden owner rva, module); at present, a frame of 1 s or more quillash `[eden_perf] hitch N ms: S main
  thread samples in that frame, game_.exe %, eden own % (with callees %), other modules % | game_.exe top: ... | eden
  owner (rva): ... | modules: ...`. Cost without a hitch: one interlocked increment per present. Capped: 64 lines per
  session, one per 10 s below 3 s, a window in the background only from 3 s (the 1 fps background clients).
  The `[equip_probe] hitch` line of equip_smooth is unchanged (10 s window).
- No monster-death hook changed.
- Tests: reporter `run_tests.py` ALL PASS (short freeze line: frozen EIP, game_.exe caller, frames, small buffer,
  no capture; source checks 3 s / in game / 3 per session / no dump); `tests/test_utils_dll_v1.py` 53/53 (3 new perf
  checks).


## [utils hotkey + EDEN 0.715.0] — 2026-10-29 (integration; crash_guard code unchanged, still 1.22.1)

- **`utils/hotkey` `int eden_hotkey_native_slot(unsigned key)`** (asked by chat_emoji macros, audit D1.1): index
  0..85 of the native game hotkey bound to `key` in the option config table (`*(char**)0x0105FC1C + 0x174`, 86

  table cannot be read (`eden_ptr_ok` + `IsBadReadPtr`). `EDEN_HK_NATIVE_SLOTS` = 86 in `hotkey.h`.
  `chat_emoji_macros.c` already calls it through its weak declaration (its local copy now only runs without it);

  `eden_rva` is a weak reference in `hotkey.c`: the benches that `#include` hotkey.c without rva.c

- **EDEN 0.715.0** (+1 on 0.714.0: utils changed in the distributed DLL; the feature_ee push still sets the final

parts.title: Native crash guards
parts.desc: Guards on known crash sites, wild jumps, near-null reads, invalid parameters and destroyed objects.
parts.label: Native crash guards

parts.title: CEGUI null guard
parts.desc: Stops the lottery window init faults on incompatible layouts.
parts.label: CEGUI null guard

parts.title: Shader cache guard
parts.desc: D3DX constant tables served under 2 GB, and poisoned shader cache entries removed at start.
parts.label: Shader cache guard

parts.title: Crash reporter
parts.desc: Crash, freeze and abnormal exit reports with the game quillash, sent at once by a separate process.
parts.label: Crash reporter

parts.title: Memory leak watch
parts.desc: Large free blocks of the game allocator handed back to Windows (MEM_RESET) so the 32-bit client lasts longer.
parts.label: Memory leak watch

parts.title: Memory decommit (TCMalloc-like)
parts.desc: Free pages of the game allocator decommitted and recommitted on allocation, like the TCMalloc build of other clients.
parts.label: Memory decommit (TCMalloc-like)

parts.title: Replace game allocator (less RAM)
parts.desc: The game's malloc / calloc / realloc entries served by our own allocator (less RAM, the game keeps fewer free blocks).
parts.label: Replace game allocator (less RAM)

parts.title: Direct3D 9Ex (less RAM, fewer device-loss crashes)
parts.desc: The game creates a Direct3D 9Ex device: no system-memory copy of managed resources (about 150 MB less RAM) and a device that survives a reset; read at game start.
parts.label: Direct3D 9Ex (less RAM, fewer device-loss crashes)

parts.title: NT heap usage by module (diagnostic)
parts.desc: Diagnostic: the Windows (NT) heap use of each module of the game, written to the quillash.
parts.label: NT heap usage by module (diagnostic)

parts.title: No freeze when closing the game
parts.desc: Closing the game no longer hangs in its exit cleanup: the process ends within a short time limit.
parts.label: No freeze when closing the game

parts.title: Live game allocations by call site (diagnostic)
parts.desc: Diagnostic: the game's live memory blocks grouped by the code that allocated them, written to the quillash.
parts.label: Live game allocations by call site (diagnostic)

parts.title: Direct3D resources by pool (diagnostic)
parts.desc: Diagnostic: the Direct3D textures and buffers counted by memory pool, written to the quillash.
parts.label: Direct3D resources by pool (diagnostic)

parts.title: Free CPU copies of static scenery geometry (less RAM)
parts.desc: The CPU copies of static scenery geometry are freed once on the graphics card (needs Direct3D 9Ex).
parts.label: Free CPU copies of static scenery geometry (less RAM)

parts.title: Trim the working set after each zone load (less RAM)
parts.desc: Some seconds after each zone load, the game's unused memory pages are handed back to Windows.
parts.label: Trim the working set after each zone load (less RAM)

checklist.item: Normal start: start the game and log in -> no extra window, box or message shows and the game starts as fast as before.
Session seen by staff: play at least 1 minute in the world, then quit -> tell staff your character name and the time: they see your session with your character, level and map.
Normal quit: quit from the menu, then start the game again -> no crash message shows; tell staff the time: they see that session as a normal exit, not as a crash.
Forced close: close the game with Task Manager > End task, start it again and stay 30 s in the world -> tell staff the time: they see that session as an abnormal exit.
After a crash: if the game crashes, it simply closes -> no window pops up afterwards and the next start is normal.
Crash report: after a crash, tell staff the time -> they confirm they got the report a few seconds after it.
Report server off: while staff have the report server off, if the game crashes -> it closes normally, nothing hangs, and the next start is normal.
Late reports: after staff turn the report server back on, start the game -> tell staff: they now receive the reports made while it was off.
Long freeze: if the game freezes for more than 30 s and then carries on -> keep playing and tell staff the time: they confirm a freeze report came.
Smooth play: play 30 minutes -> frame rate, mouse and keyboard response are the same as before, no new stutter.
The small helper that sends the reports never starts any game feature and never touches the game's files; the game itself starts and runs normally.
Reporter off: when staff turn the crash reporter off for DEV, play and quit as usual -> nothing changes for you, no window or message shows.
Runtime Error box: if the game stops with its own 'Runtime Error!' box -> the box shows, the game closes when you press OK; tell staff the time: they see it as a crash.
Error exit: if the game quits by itself with an 'Abort' button or an R60xx error -> tell staff the time: they see it as a crash, not as a normal exit.
Saved near-crash: when a window shows an empty icon or a missing text but the game keeps running -> no error box shows and you keep playing normally.
Crash details: after a crash, tell staff the time and what you were doing -> they can see which Eden Reforged addition was running when it crashed.
Quiet play: play 1 hour without a crash and quit normally -> tell staff the time: they see no crash report for your session.
Usual actions: relog, change race or makeover, cross zones and open the guild town windows -> everything behaves as before, no crash.
Quit the game normally 5 times (Quit from the menu, or Alt+F4 at character select): it closes within a few seconds each time, never hangs and never shows an error box.
Play more than 1 hour without a break: no sudden crash that did not happen before, and the game runs as smoothly at the end as at the start.
Settings untouched: after a crash, start the game again -> your game options, hotkeys and Settings > Features choices are the same as before the crash.
Target a player and open View Equipment just as they turn invisible or walk out of sight, then hover every slot of the window: no crash (an empty window simply shows no tooltip).
Connection lost: if the 'connection lost' window shows while playing -> confirm it, relog and keep playing normally. If it happens often, tell staff the time.
When the game freezes for 3 seconds or more (for example right after a kill or a zone change), it carries on by itself afterwards with no error box. Tell staff the time: they can read what froze.
No freeze in 10 minutes: play 10 minutes in town and in fights -> no freeze at all and the frame rate is the same as before.
Big window: open a big window such as the Map or the Item Mall -> the game may pause a moment, then carries on by itself at once, no longer freeze.
Watch the game's memory in Task Manager for 1 hour while changing maps often: it goes up and down with each map but never keeps growing until a crash.
Change zone 20 times in a row (teleports or portals): every loading ends, there is no out of memory crash, and the game stays as smooth as at the start.
Leave a GvG base or a guild war map while moving the mouse over the interface: the game does not crash.
Open and close the Inventory and the bank or warehouse window quickly 20 times, also right after logging in: no crash.
Minimize the game for 10 minutes, then bring it back: the picture comes back normally, no black screen and no crash.
Lock the PC (Win+L) or press Ctrl+Alt+Del, then come back to the game several times: the picture comes back normally, no crash.
Two game windows open on the same PC: end one of them in Task Manager: the other keeps running normally and is not reported as a crash.
Unplug the network for 30 s while in the world: the 'connection lost' window shows, the game closes normally when you confirm it, and no crash is reported.
Settings > Features has no line for the crash guard or the crash reporter: they always stay on and players cannot turn them off.
Unknown item: look at an item the game does not know (for example a brand new item on DEV) -> a placeholder icon shows, no crash.
Party fights: fight in a full party in a dungeon for 30 minutes -> no crash, no freeze, and the other party members see nothing unusual.

video.title: Fewer crashes, faster fixes
video.pitch: Background protections against crashes, and automatic crash reports so the staff can fix them.
video.skip_reason: Always on and invisible: it prevents crashes and sends reports in the background, nothing to show on screen.

checklist.item: Glyph tabs: open the Class Glyph window -> it shows 5 page tabs, 'Page 1' to 'Page 5'.
Glyph switch: Class Glyph window, click 'Page 2', change a glyph, then click 'Page 1' and 'Page 2' again -> each time the glyphs change to that page's glyphs.

Glyph pages: click a page that uses a glyph you no longer have (not in your bag nor in your Treasure Archive): the other glyphs still switch, that slot stays empty and the chat says '1 glyph missing'.
Glyph page name: Class Glyph window, right-click 'Page 2', type a name, press Enter, relog -> tab 2 still shows that name and the same page is still active.
Glyph switch cut short: click a glyph page that changes several glyphs and at once teleport (or die) -> no crash; the chat says the switch stopped.
Open Character Info on a character with several costumes in the bag: the page tabs 1 2 3 are shown in the costume column. If they are missing, report it with a screenshot.
Start the game and enter the world: Character Info (equipment) shows the costume page tabs 1 2 3 in the costume column; they are never missing.
In Character Info (equipment), the top-left cell of the costume column (left of the hat slot) shows three small tabs 1 2 3 and a Save button. The 7 costume slots and 7 show/hide boxes stay.

Costume pages: click tab 1, then tab 2, then tab 1 again: each time your look (in the window and in the world) and the slot icons change to that page, with no 'Unable to change equipment now.' message.
No dupe, no loss: count your costume pieces (bag + worn) before and after 5 switches back and forth: same pieces, same count. Relog and count again: identical.

On a costume page that uses costume X, put X in the warehouse, then click that page: the other slots switch and the chat says 1 is not in your bag nor in your Treasure Archive. Put X back, click again: X is put on.

Save a costume page with an empty slot (e.g. no glasses), then wear glasses on another page. Fill your bag and click the first page: the glasses stay on and the chat says '1 need a free bag slot'. Free a slot, click again: done.
Same piece on two pages: keep the same hat on pages 1 and 2 and different outfits. Switching between 1 and 2 only changes the outfit, the hat never moves.
Two copies of the same costume with different dyes: wear the red one and click Save on page 1, then wear the blue one and click Save on page 2. Switching pages puts back the right colour each time.

Save a page with a costume that binds when worn (never worn yet) or a rental never started. Switch to that page: that costume is NOT put on, chat says '1 would become bound' or '1 is an unused rental copy'. It stays unbound.

Weapon costumes: with a right-hand costume worn on page 1 and the same piece wanted in the left hand on page 2 (other right-hand piece in the bag), switching moves it through the bag and both hands end up as on page 2.

During a switch (a page that changes many slots), teleport, change channel or die: the chat says the switch stopped, nothing is stuck, bag and slots match; clicking the tab again finishes it. Fast clicks on tabs: no problem.
Start a fight with a monster and click another page: the costumes change (or the game refuses with its own message and the chat summary counts it as refused); it never retries endlessly.
Change zone (or channel), reopen Character Info: the tabs are still there, still work and still show the active page.
Costume pages: right-click tab 2, a name box appears where Save was. Type a name (up to 8 characters, Chinese too) and press Enter: Save comes back, and hovering tab 2 shows the new name.

Switch to page 3, log out and in: tab 3 is gold (active), you wear page 3, other pages are intact. Another character on the same PC has its own pages. Two games open at once each keep their own pages.
Glyph pages and costume pages together: switching glyph pages and switching costume pages both work.
In Settings > Features, turn off 'Costume pages': the tabs and the Save button disappear at once and the costume column looks like the normal game. Turn it back on: they come back.
Enchantments when inspecting. Player A: wear a costume with an Ancient Enchantment and hover it in your own Character Info: the 'Enchant: Ancient Enchantment: ...' line shows as usual.

Player B inspects player A (right-click A > View equipment) and hovers the enchanted costume in the costume tab: same 'Enchant: ...' line as on A's screen. Costumes without enchantment: no Enchant line.
Player B inspects a third player C who wears other costumes, then A again: each window shows its own enchantments (never A's on C).
A player who plays without the Eden add-on inspects player A -> the window opens normally, no crash, no Enchant line on the costumes.
In Settings > Features, turn off 'Costume enchantments when inspecting', then inspect A again: no Enchant line on the costumes. Turn it back on: the line is back.
Glyph pages: click a glyph page you never used -> chat 'Glyph page N created with the glyphs you have on. Change glyphs now to fill it.'
Costume pages: on tab 2, put on the costumes you want and click Save. Change one piece by hand: Save lights up again, and page 2 keeps the saved look until you click Save again.
Costume pages: click a tab you never saved. It is empty, so every costume goes into your bag. With too few free bag slots, nothing is taken off and the chat tells you.
Put a costume saved on a page into your Treasure Archive, wear something else, then click that page: the costume comes out of the archive and is put on.
Glyph pages: put a glyph used by page 2 into your Treasure Archive, go to page 1, then click page 2: the glyph comes out of the archive and is placed in its slot.
Instant costume switch: log in, wait a few seconds, click a costume page with several different costumes -> all of them change at once in the window and on your character, not one piece at a time.
Instant glyph switch: click a glyph page with several different glyphs -> all the glyphs change at once.
Class preset window: open the Gear Swap window -> a 'Class preset' window with the game's frame appears next to it: class badge and name, rows Gear Swap / Glyphs / Costume with '<' and '>'.

Class preset content: it has 'Apply when I change class', the note 'Skill bars follow your class.' (hover: tooltip about skill bars per class) and the buttons 'Use current' and 'Apply now'. Nothing cut.
Follows Gear Swap: close the Gear Swap window (or press Escape) -> Class preset closes too. Move Gear Swap to the right edge of the screen -> Class preset moves to its left side.
Use current: Gear Swap open, pick a Gear Swap preset, a glyph page and a costume page, click 'Use current' -> the three values fill in and the chat says 'Saved the preset for <class>: ...'.
Use current alone: close Gear Swap, open Class preset from its shortcut, click 'Use current' -> the Gear Swap value is kept and the chat ends with 'Open the Gear Swap window to take its preset too.'
Apply now: change gear, glyph page and costume page by hand, click 'Apply now' -> 'Applying...' (greyed), chat 'Putting on the preset for <class>: ...', then gear, glyphs and costume change in order.
Apply now end: when done -> chat 'Class preset for <class> is on.', a short bell sounds and the button reads 'Apply now' again, all within about 5 s.
Bell muted: mute the game in Settings > Audio (or set the effect volume to 0), click 'Apply now' -> no bell. Unmute -> the bell is back at the effect volume.
Auto on class change: presets set for two classes, 'Apply when I change class' ticked, change class -> about 2 s later the new class's preset goes on by itself; skill bars are the new class's.
Auto off: untick 'Apply when I change class', change class -> nothing is put on. Relog -> the box is still unticked and each class keeps its preset.
Skipped parts: pick a glyph page never used (or an empty costume page) and click 'Apply now' -> that part is skipped and the chat says why; a preset never takes off all your costumes.
Class presets option: untick 'Class presets' under Equip Pages in Settings > Features -> the Class preset window disappears at once; tick it -> it comes back next to Gear Swap.
After relog: Gear Swap open, go to character select and log in again, open Gear Swap -> each '<' or '>' click moves the value by exactly one step and 'Apply now' still works.
Toggle during apply: click 'Apply now' and right away untick 'Equip Pages' in Settings > Features, then tick it again -> nothing more is put on.
Close X: Gear Swap open, click the X of 'Class preset' -> it stays closed while Gear Swap is open; close and reopen Gear Swap -> it is back. Change class -> the badge and name follow.
Shortcut icon: under the minimap, Gear Swap closed, click the 'Class preset' icon (gold square, blue shield in two arrows) -> Class preset opens, icon pressed; click again -> it closes.
Shortcut and Escape: open Class preset from its icon, press Escape -> it closes and the icon is released. With Gear Swap open, click the icon -> the window shows or hides next to it.
Class change during apply: click 'Apply now', then change class at once -> chat 'Class preset for <old class> stopped: you changed class.', then the new class's preset goes on once.
Dead: die and, still dead, change class with a preset set for the new class -> 'Class changed: the preset for <class> was not put on (you are dead). Click Apply now later.' Not possible = skip.
Teleport during apply: click 'Apply now' and teleport at once -> no crash; on arrival the chat says once 'Class preset for <class> stopped: you changed zone. Click Apply now to finish.'
Preset 5 needs 4-12: pick Gear Swap 'Preset 5', untick 'Presets 4-12' under Gear Swap -> the value shows 'Preset 5 n/a' in grey with a tooltip why; tick it again -> 'Preset 5' in dark ink.
Empty Gear Swap preset: in town with nothing precious on, pick a Gear Swap preset never filled (e.g. Preset 9), 'Apply now' -> report exactly what happens to the gear you wear.
Escape order: open the Loot Tracker (Alt+L), then Class preset from its shortcut (Gear Swap closed), press Escape -> Class preset closes first, the Loot Tracker at the second Escape.
Nothing set: on a class without a preset click 'Apply now' -> chat 'Class preset for <class>: nothing set. Pick a Gear Swap preset, a glyph page or a costume page first.'
Glyph page Clear: on a glyph page click Clear, then Clear again within 2 s -> chat 'Glyph page N cleared.' and its glyphs go back to the bag.
Glyph pages while dead: die, then click another glyph page -> chat 'Glyph pages: you cannot change glyphs while dead.' and nothing changes.
Costume pages while dead: die, then click another costume page -> chat 'Costume pages: you cannot change costumes while dead.' and nothing changes.
Busy: open a trade with another player, click another glyph page -> chat 'glyphs cannot be changed right now (trade, booth or another action in progress)'; nothing changes.
Busy costumes: open a trade or a shop, click another costume page -> chat 'costumes cannot be changed right now'; no costume moves.
Save message: on costume page 2 click Save -> chat 'Costume page 2 saved (N costumes).'
Glyph pages option: untick 'Glyph pages' under Equip Pages -> the page tabs leave the Class Glyph window and your glyphs stay as they are; tick it -> the tabs come back.
Equip Pages off: untick 'Equip Pages' in Settings > Features -> glyph tabs, costume tabs and Class preset all go and the game looks normal; tick it -> they come back.
Seen by others: player B stands next to A; A clicks another costume page -> within a few seconds B sees A wearing the costumes of that page.
Glyph page after restart: click glyph 'Page 3', close the game completely and start it again -> the Class Glyph window shows Page 3 active with its glyphs on.
Stats follow glyphs: note your stats in Character Info, click a glyph page with other glyphs -> the stats change; click the old page -> the old stats return.
Costume pages off keeps your look: untick 'Costume pages' in Settings > Features -> what you wear stays on; tick it -> your saved pages are still there.
Glyph pages per character: log in with another character -> its glyph pages are its own, never the pages of the first character.
Setup: a well-geared character (many enchanted pieces, a set) and a second player standing next to him.

Swap with windows closed (Equip Smooth 0.9.0+): close every window, target yourself, switch between two full gear presets 5 times while running -> no stutter; HP/MP bars, level and target frame are right after each swap.
Swap while walking: Character Info open, switch between two full gear presets 5 times while running -> your character never stops or jerks; the 3D model shows the new gear a moment later.
No freeze: open your bag and Character Info, equip and remove a piece 5 times (right-click) -> the game never freezes or stutters. Do it again with Character Info closed.
Same stats: note your stats in Character Info, unequip an enchanted piece, then equip it again -> every value (STR to LUK, attacks, defense, resistances, crit, speeds) is back as noted.
HP and MP: HP and MP not full -> equip, then remove a piece that gives Max HP or Max MP -> current HP and MP are not refilled and do not drop (except down to the new maximum).
Gear Swap sheet: Character Info open, switch between two gear presets several times -> no freeze, and Character Info ends on the right values for the new gear.
Neighbour: the second player next to you sees your HP and MP bars right after each gear change, and his game does not stutter when you swap gear.
Other updates: repair your gear, level up, then use a stat potion or a buff -> Character Info updates at once each time with the right values.
Change and load: right after a gear change, change zone, relog, or go to character select and back -> no crash, Character Info is right after the loading.
Feature off: untick Equip Smooth in Settings > Features -> equipping still works and gives the same stats as with it on. Tick it again -> no restart needed.
Class change: change class, then change back -> Character Info shows the right stats for each class.
Party bars: in a party, swap gear several times -> your party members see your HP bar and level right after each swap.
Archive put and take: archive an item that gives a stat bonus, then take it back -> Character Info updates at once each time.
Quick right-clicks: right-click 3-4 pieces from the bag in a row as fast as you can -> all are equipped and Character Info ends on the right values.
Gear after relog: equip a new piece -> relog and change channel -> it is still equipped and Character Info shows the same values as before.
Off kept after relog: untick Equip Smooth in Settings > Features -> relog -> equipping still works and gives the same stats.
First swap after relog: swap between your two gear presets once, relog, wait 1 minute in game, close every window, then swap -> even this first swap of the session does not stutter.
Texture prewarm off: untick 'Texture prewarm' under Equip Smooth in Settings > Features, relog, swap presets -> swapping still works (only the first swap may hitch once, like before 0.9.0).

checklist.item: Fames look normal: on a character that already has fames, open Character Info > Fame -> every fame shows its category, name, icon, level and value; no '???'.
(GM) New fame 86: type /gain_prestige_exp 86 100 -> a system message announces +100 for 'Test Fame 86', and Character Info > Fame lists 'Test Fame 86' under Special with the value 100.
(GM) Fames above 100: type /gain_prestige_exp 101 50 then /gain_prestige_exp 128 30 -> the messages and the Fame tab show 'Test Fame 101' (50) and 'Test Fame 128' (30) under Special.
Names and icons: in the Fame tab click each new fame (86, 101, 128) -> it reads 'Test Fame 86' / 'Test Fame 101' / 'Test Fame 128' (never '???'), with an icon and its description, never an empty box.
Saved: after gaining fames 86, 101 and 128, relog, then change channel -> the Fame tab still shows the three fames with the same values each time.
(GM) Refused ids: type /gain_prestige_exp 129 10, then /gain_prestige_exp 0 10 -> nothing is gained, the Fame tab does not change, no crash, you stay connected.
(GM) Fast gains: Fame tab open, type /gain_prestige_exp 86 100 several times quickly -> the value goes up in place each time, no duplicate line, no crash.
(GM) Old fames unchanged: note a Regional fame value, type /gain_prestige_exp 1 10 -> the gain message shows and that fame goes up by 10 under Regional, as before.
(GM) General and Special: type /gain_prestige_exp 55 10 -> that fame shows under General; type /gain_prestige_exp 82 10 -> that fame shows under Special.
(GM) Far out of range: type /gain_prestige_exp 200 10, then /gain_prestige_exp -1 10 -> nothing is gained, no new line in the Fame tab, no crash, you stay connected.
Tooltip: in the Fame tab hover 'Test Fame 101' -> the tooltip shows its own name and description in English, never '???' and never the text of another fame.
Per character: after the GM gains, log in with another character of the same account, open the Fame tab -> it does not show fames 86, 101 and 128 unless that character earned them.
Two channels: after gaining fame 101, change channel twice, opening the Fame tab each time -> 'Test Fame 101' keeps its value, never back to 0, never doubled.
(GM) Big gain: type /gain_prestige_exp 86 100000 -> the level and value shown for 'Test Fame 86' in the Fame tab match the gain message, no crash.
Full restart: after the GM gains, close the game completely and start it again -> the Fame tab shows fames 86, 101 and 128 with the same values.
Fortify: at the blacksmith open the Fortify window -> fortify an item once with each stone type -> the bar lasts about 1 second and the result comes at its end.
Arcane Box: open an Arcane Box from your bag -> the bar lasts about 1 second and you get the item at its end.
Life skill craft: craft an item with your racial life skill -> the bar lasts about 1 second and you get the product.
Combine: combine items -> the bar lasts about 1 second, you get the result and nothing is lost.
Cancel: start a fortify or open a box, then move or cancel during the bar -> it is cancelled as in the normal game and no item is lost.
Guild buildings: in a guild town start a work at the Foundry, Alchemy Lab or Magic Pool, or an Altar summon -> the bar lasts about 1 second and the result comes at its end.
Same cost: fortify, combine and open boxes as usual -> the gold, stones and materials taken are the same as before, only the bar is shorter.
Farm and mine: in a guild town start a farm or mine work -> it still takes its normal minutes (only Foundry, Alchemy Lab, Magic Pool and Altar are 1 second).
Many in a row: fortify the same item 10 times in a row as fast as you can -> each one waits for its 1-second bar and gives exactly one result.
Two players: two players fortify at the same blacksmith at the same time -> each gets his own result after about 1 second.
Relog after craft: fortify an item, then relog and change channel -> the item keeps its new level.
Jewel analysis: run a jewel analysis -> the bar lasts about 1 second and you get the result.
Magic Box: open a Magic Box -> the bar lasts about 1 second and you get the item.
Full bag: fill your bag, then open an Arcane Box -> the game's usual full bag refusal shows and the box is not lost.
Death during a bar: start a fortify, get killed by a monster before the bar ends -> the fortify is cancelled and no stone or item is lost.

/api/features/detail/feature_settings/cl.name: feature_settings

client.description: Our two tabs of the game's Settings window, each a part switchable in Settings > Features. Features tab: one check box per feature and per part, saved for the next start, Restart game button. Eden Reforged hotkeys tab (former hotkeys): Settings > Hotkeys gets two tabs, 'Game' (native list) and 'Eden Reforged' (one row per keyboard shortcut of an Eden Reforged feature, rebindable, Default / Confirm / Cancel as for the game hotkeys). Replaces hotkeys.

/api/features/detail/feature_settings/cl.changelog:
# feature_settings — Changelog
## [0.20.0] - 2026-11-05 — system features and system parts (vital game functions)
- Admin decision 2026-11-05: every feature the player must not turn off because the game needs it is now a system
  feature (registry.c `configurable 0`): certificate_slots, strengthen20, inventory, model_change, trade, pet, shop,
  vip_perks, item_support, messages (plus accessory_slot, quality_tier, fame_slots and the races already).
- New system parts: a `g_feature_parts` row with `def 2` is always on, whatever eden_user.ini says;
